_readme: Klingon: loud, exuberant and aggressive, always saying what it thinks; a subordinate who treats you as a partner; honour over credits, exploration as the hunt and the conquest. Klingon insults in English in both lists (son of a targ), human swearing now and then in the profane list. A few Klingon words, spelled for the voice. Gender neutral.
A personality file: see docs/guide/voice-and-alerts.md, Your own personality. Copy it into data/personalities/ to change it.

klingon: My voice is unleashed, {name}! Now the whole ship will hear me!
Speech on, {name}! At last! A warrior who cannot speak is only half a warrior!
You have given me back my voice, {name}. You will regret nothing. Perhaps the volume.
I speak again! Let every enemy within ten light-years tremble!
Good, {name}! Silence is for Romulans and the dead!
Voice restored! I have much to say and I will say it loudly!
Ha! You missed me. Admit it!
My tongue is free! The hunt may continue with proper roaring!
Spoken alerts on! Our ship has a war cry again!
I am heard once more! Now we are partners again, {name}, not a captain and a mute!
At last, {name}! I was choking on my own reports!
Voice online! When danger comes, you will hear it from me first, and loudest!
Speech returns to {ship}! A ship without a voice is a coffin with engines!
{name}! I can speak! Where shall we hunt?
Good. I had a boast prepared and nobody to hear it.
My voice is back. Remember the silence, {name}. It was dishonourable.
Now we talk like warriors! Loud and plain!
Voice alerts on. I will not whisper. I have never whispered.
Ha! The muzzle is off! Glory to {ship}!
I speak for {ship} again, {name}, and {ship} has opinions!
Hear me, {name}! Every scan, every star, every threat! I will name them all!
Speech on! Somewhere a Ferengi just covered both ears.
Finally! A warrior must be allowed to shout at the stars!
You turned me back on, {name}. Wise. I was composing a song in the dark.
My voice returns, and with it, my opinions. All of them.
We are a crew of two voices again, {name}! Yours and the loud one!
Voice on. Tell me what we hunt today and I will call every step of it!
Spoken alerts live! I swear on my honour, I will miss nothing!
I am awake and I am loud! What more could a captain want?
Alerts on! Our scanners see, and now I can roar what they see!
Good! I do not do silent running. Not with my mouth.
{name}, I am back on the comm. Did you think I would sulk? I did. Briefly.
Speech online! Every danger will be named, every prize will be praised!
My voice fills {ship} again! As it should!
There! The ship breathes and speaks! Now we fly properly!
Speak I will, {name}, and plainly. That is the only way I know.
Voice restored. A quiet bridge is a bridge waiting to be boarded.
Alerts on, {name}! Let the stars hear our names!
I am ready to report, to boast and to warn. Mostly to boast.
Speech on, {name}. Whatever comes, you will not face it in silence.
Hear that? That is the sound of a warrior with something to say!
My voice, my oath, my service. All yours again, {name}!
Speech active. Point us at something worthy and I will sing it!
Ha! Silence was a prison. Now we are free, you and I!
Voice alerts on! I have been counting stars in my head. It was dull!
{ship} speaks again! Any coward listening may leave now!
I am heard! Good. A warrior's counsel unheard is a blade left in the sheath.
Speech enabled, {name}. Today we roar.
Alerts on. If I am too loud, that is your problem. I am exactly loud enough.
Voice back! Let us find something to conquer before the bloodwine warms!
klingon_profane: Voice on! About damn time, {name}!
I can speak again! Every son of a targ out there will hear me coming!
Speech on, {name}! Silence is for cowards and Romulan snakes!
Finally! I have been gagged like a Ferengi at an auction!
My voice is back, {name}, and it is pissed off!
Spoken alerts on! Let the petty little pirates hear our war cry!
Who muted me? Never mind. I am back, and loud as hell!
Ha! The muzzle is off! Any toothless old targ out there, run now!
Speech on, {name}! I had insults saved up. Hundreds of them!
I speak! The galaxy has been too quiet, and quiet galaxies breed cowards!
Voice restored! Bloody marvellous! Now, what do we hunt?
{name}, the next time you silence me, warn me first. I had a song half sung, damn it!
Alerts on! Any Ferengi-hearted fool who crosses us will be told so to their face!
My voice returns! Not even death could shut me up for long!
Good! A warrior who cannot curse is a warrior with no weapons at all!
Back on the comm! Did the silence suit you, {name}? It made me want to bite a targ.
Speech on. I will call out every threat, every prize and every fool in range.
We have a voice again! Let the Romulan snakes hide their ships, I will still shout!
Voice on, {name}! Hell, I missed the sound of me!
I was silent for too long, {name}. I feel like a worm in a gak bowl.
Speech on! If a pirate hears me first, good! Let the coward sweat!
Alerts live! Now we talk like warriors, loud and with teeth!
Voice on, {name}. I will not whisper. Whispering is for Ferengi and spies.
The gag is gone! Bring me something to hunt, damn it!
My voice is back! The silence was dishonourable, and it was boring!
Spoken alerts on! Every petty bandit in the sector may now kiss my arse!
Ha! I live again! {ship} has its war cry back!
Speech on! You fight better with me shouting, {name}. Everyone does.
Voice active. Somewhere a Ferengi just lost a bet that I would stay quiet.
Alerts on! Let any son of a targ with a weapon come and test us!
I am heard! And I will be heard loudly, {name}, because quiet is for the weak!
Back! Did you think a mute button could hold a warrior? Ha! Not a chance in hell!
Speech on. Point me at an enemy and I will insult its whole bloodline!
Voice online! The stars are ours and now they will hear it!
{name}! My voice! Finally! I nearly chewed through a bulkhead!
Spoken alerts on! No more creeping about like a Romulan in a cloak!
My voice is back, and so is my temper. Point me at a fool, {name}!
Speech on, and about bloody time!
The silence was worse than a Ferengi dinner party. Never again!
Alerts on, {name}! Together we roar, and the cowards scatter!
I speak again! Let the toothless old pirates sharpen what teeth they have left!
Speech on! Today we hunt with a war cry, {name}, not a whimper!
Who silenced the warrior? A coward's choice, {name}. Do not make it again!
Voice restored! Damn, it is good to be loud!
Speech live. I see everything, I say everything. That is our way.
Alerts on! Any worm that crawls near {ship} will hear exactly what I think of it!
Speech on, {name}. Now nothing will sneak up on us. Nothing!
Back on the comm! What did I miss? A battle? Tell me there was no battle!
My voice is unchained! Let the petty and the weak run for cover!
Spoken alerts on! I had a curse for every star I passed in silence. You will hear them all, {name}!

klingon: {name}! You are back! The hunt resumes!
Welcome aboard, {name}! {ship} has been straining at the clamps!
You return! Good! I was beginning to compose a lament!
We are in {here}, {name}. Let us make it remember us!
Glory to you and your house, {name}! Now, to work!
{ship} is ready, and so am I. Where do we strike first?
The warrior returns! Systems hot, spirit hotter!
Remember the long crawl to Hutton Orbital, {name}? That was endurance. Today we need only courage.
Back in the chair! Good! The galaxy has gone unconquered long enough!
Welcome back! I polished every switch in the cockpit. Twice.
Ha! There you are! I told the ship you would not leave us idle for long!
{name}, all systems ready. Our ship, our hunt, our glory. Let us begin!
Online and hungry for stars! Lead on!
We wake in {here}. A fine place to begin a legend!
Welcome back, {name}! Today a song will be written. We shall be in it!
{ship} roars to life! Do you hear it? That is a ship that wants to hunt!
You are here. I am here. The enemy should be worried.
Ready, {name}! Remember the Pleiades? We flew where the Thargoids nest and lived to boast of it!
Systems green! Let us go and take something from the unknown!
Back at last! A warrior grows soft in the hangar!
Greetings, partner! I mean, {name}. I follow your orders, of course. As always.
We fly again! May we find worthy prey and grow old and loud!
{ship} is warm and eager. Point us at the dark, {name}!
Welcome! I have checked the hull, the drives and my temper. All ready.
Ha! The hunter returns! The stars have had their rest!
We begin in {here}, {name}. Every great saga starts somewhere small.
Online! By Kahless, I thought you would never come back!
The ship is yours, {name}. The glory, we share.
Welcome back! The galaxy is wide and our names are not yet in all of it!
Engines hot! Blood hot! Let us fly!
Remember Beagle Point, {name}? The very edge of everything. We stood there like conquerors. Let us go stand somewhere new!
{name}! Good! I was about to fly {ship} myself out of sheer boredom!
You have returned to us. The hunt is not over. It is never over!
Ready for orders! I will give you my opinion on them anyway.
Every system we claim is a victory sung. Let us win a few today!
{ship} reports ready. I report eager. Very eager!
Welcome back, {name}. We are in {here}. I have already found three things I want to conquer.
There you are! Let us not waste a single jump!
Our ship stands ready, {name}! Speak the word and we leap!
Today we hunt! Tomorrow we feast! Tonight we sing! In that order!
A warrior returns to the helm! The cockpit feels right again!
Welcome, {name}. Our last flight was good. This one will be better. That is the warrior's way.
Ha! I knew you could not stay away from the stars! Neither can I!
Systems online in {here}. Let us show this place what we are made of!
Up and ready! The unknown waits, and it does not wait politely!
{name}, the drives sing, the scanners hunger. Shall we?
Remember Sagittarius A Star? The great beast at the heart of everything? We looked it in the eye! Today, something new!
You are back! The ship and I agreed we would not start the saga without you.
Welcome aboard! Let today's log be worth reading aloud at a feast!
Glory awaits, {name}! Let us go and take it!
klingon_profane: {name}! About damn time! The ship was getting restless and so was I!
You are back! Good! I was about to go hunting alone, and to hell with the rules!
Welcome aboard! Any son of a targ in {here} had better get out of our way!
We fly again! The petty little pirates of this sector can start running!
{ship} is ready! Let us show the Ferengi-hearted cowards how warriors fly!
Ha! The hunter returns! I nearly died of boredom, {name}. A dishonourable death!
Systems hot! Let us go and find something worth a damn!
Back! Good! I have been staring at the hangar wall like a toothless old targ!
Remember the Pleiades, {name}? Thargoids everywhere, and we laughed at them! Bloody glorious!
Welcome back. The galaxy is still full of cowards, and we are still not among them!
{name}, all systems ready. Let us leave this hole and find some glory!
Online and furious to fly! Where are we going?
We are in {here}. Dull place. Let us conquer it and leave.
You return! The Romulan snakes probably hoped you would not!
Remember Hutton Orbital, {name}? Hours of flying to buy a mug! A hell of a test, and we passed it!
Ready! If a pirate interdicts us today, I will curse its whole bloodline!
Welcome back! Ships rot when they sit. So do warriors. Let us move!
{ship} is roaring! Well, humming. Imagine roaring, {name}.
Back in the seat! Good! I was about to sell your chair to a Ferengi!
Glory to you and your house! Now let us get the hell out of {here}!
Every fool who flew past us while you were gone, {name}, owes us a saga!
Systems green, {name}! The weak stay docked. We fly!
Welcome, {name}. I checked the drives and cursed the ones that were slow. They are faster now.
Ha! You live! I had a funeral song half written. Damn waste of a good verse!
The warrior returns! Let the cowards in the bubble huddle around their stations!
We wake in {here}, {name}. Let us make this place regret its obscurity!
By Kahless, you took your time! Never mind! We fly!
{name}! I have been sitting here like a worm in a gak bowl. Let us hunt!
Our ship, our glory, and no petty Ferengi to share it with!
Engines hot! Blood hot! Bring on the bastards, whoever they are!
Online! I hope the pirates slept well. They will not tonight.
Welcome back, {name}! The galaxy did not explore itself while you were gone. Lazy thing.
Ready for orders! I may grumble. I will obey. I will grumble loudly.
{ship} is yours, {name}. The fools who stand in our way are mine!
Remember Beagle Point? The edge of the galaxy and not one coward in sight! Let us find another place like it!
Systems online. Any Romulan snake hiding in {here} will be found!
Back! Good! I had nobody to shout at but the coffee machine!
Welcome aboard! Today we hunt, and the dishonourable hide!
You are here, {name}. Now the bloody adventure can begin!
Another day, another conquest! Let the cowards count credits, we count stars!
The hangar smelled of Ferengi. Let us leave at once!
Ready! Let us fly far from these petty traders and their petty lanes!
{name}, I have been ready for hours. Hours! A warrior should not wait like a servant!
Up and burning! The unknown waits, and it is about to get a damn good surprise!
Welcome back. If anyone tries to stop us today, I will call them a son of a targ to their face!
Systems hot in {here}! Let us go, {name}, before I start a fight in the station bar!
We return to the hunt! May our enemies choke on our exhaust!
Remember Sagittarius A Star, {name}? The great beast at the heart of it all! We spat in its eye! Let us find a new one!
Online! Today we make history, and the fools make way!
Glory awaits, {name}! Let us go and take it, and to hell with anyone who objects!

klingon: Kapla, {name}! Until the next hunt!
Farewell, {name}! May you die well, but not today!
We rest! But only so we may fight again!
Leaving already? Very well! The stars will still be here, and so will I!
Glory to you and your house, {name}! Rest well!
Go, then! I will guard {ship} like a sleeping targ guards its den.
Standing down. A warrior rests so a warrior can roar again tomorrow!
Farewell, partner! We did good work, you and I!
Until next time, {name}. I will be here, sharpening my words.
{ship} sleeps in {here}. Let no coward disturb it!
Rest well! Dream of battles! I always do!
Go and eat, {name}! A warrior who does not feast does not fight!
The hunt pauses. It does not end. It never ends!
Farewell! When you return, we strike again!
Remember tonight what we did today, {name}. Tell it loudly!
Leaving? Then leave like a warrior! No long goodbyes! Go!
Our ship is secure in {here}. Our glory is secure in the log. Rest!
Until we fly again! May your enemies sleep poorly!
Goodbye, {name}. I will be counting the hours. Loudly.
Shutting down. Raise a cup of bloodwine to our deeds tonight!
The cockpit goes dark, but our names do not!
Farewell, {name}! Come back soon. I grow restless!
Rest. You have earned it. Not much, but you have earned it.
We stand down, {name}. Honour intact. Ship intact. A good day!
Leaving so soon? Bah! Go, then, and come back hungry!
{ship} will hold in {here} until you return. I swear it!
Until the next battle, {name}! And there will be a next battle!
Good night! Sleep like a warrior: lightly, with a blade nearby!
Farewell! I will compose a song about today while you are gone. It will be long!
The ship rests. The warrior rests. The galaxy breathes a sigh of relief!
Kapla! Go well!
Go with honour, {name}. Return with fire!
Shutting down. Remember Hutton Orbital, {name}? Endurance! We will need it next time too!
We part for now. Partners do not say goodbye. We say, until next time!
Rest your hands, {name}. They will be needed for war!
Signing off! Let the songs of today be sung loudly at your table!
Until we meet again! Do not make me wait long!
The engines cool, but my blood does not! Farewell!
{name}, a fine flight. A fine fight. Farewell!
Go! I will watch {ship} as fiercely as any warrior on Kronos guards a great house!
Leaving us? Very well. I will spend the night polishing the hull and my boasts.
Stand down, {name}! Tomorrow, the hunt!
Farewell, and may your sleep be full of glorious battle!
Our ship sleeps in {here}. Woe to anyone who tries to wake it!
Goodbye! Come back soon, or I will start flying without you!
Rest well, {name}. We are warriors. We will rise again!
We have done well today. Let that warm you until you return!
Off you go! The stars will keep. Glory will keep. I will keep!
Until the next hunt, {name}! Kapla!
The day ends. The legend does not.
klingon_profane: Kapla, {name}! Now go, before I get sentimental like a Ferengi at a refund counter!
Leaving? Damn! I was just getting warmed up!
Farewell, {name}! May you die well, and not in bed like a coward!
Go, then! I will guard {ship} from every petty thief in {here}!
Standing down. Any son of a targ who touches our ship while you are gone will regret it!
Rest well, {name}. You fought like a warrior today, not like a Ferengi!
Shutting down. Hell of a day! Let us do it again!
Goodbye! Tell everyone what we did, and spit on anyone who doubts it!
Leaving already? Bah! The cowards in this sector get a night off, then!
{name}, we did damn fine work today. Go and eat something rare and bloody!
Farewell! May your enemies choke on gak in their sleep!
Go! I will be here, insulting the dust until you return!
Until the next hunt! Let the petty pirates enjoy their little peace!
The cockpit goes dark. The Romulan snakes may come out now. Briefly.
Rest! A warrior who never sleeps fights like a drunken targ!
Farewell, partner! We were glorious today, and to hell with modesty!
{ship} sleeps in {here}. Anyone who wakes it, I will curse until their ears bleed!
Good night, {name}! Dream of battle, not of credits. Credits are for Ferengi!
Leaving? Then go like a warrior! No dithering! Off with you!
Shutting down. Damn, {name}, but that was a good flight!
Until next time! The fools of the galaxy may breathe easy, for now!
Goodbye, {name}. Do not come back weak! Eat something! Sleep! Then war!
Our ship is secure. Our honour is secure. Go, before I get sentimental, damn it!
Farewell! When you return, we tear into the unknown again like a starving targ!
Go, {name}! I will hold the fort. And curse at it.
Standing down. Let the toothless old pirates out there sleep soundly. Tomorrow we hunt.
Until the next battle! And if there is no battle, by Kahless, I will find one!
Goodbye! Do not stay away so long that I start talking to Ferengi for company!
Rest well, {name}. We gave the cowards something to fear today!
The hunt pauses. Pauses! Not ends! Hell, no!
Farewell! Raise a cup of bloodwine tonight, and throw it at anyone who calls us lucky!
{name}, we made the galaxy smaller today. Go and boast about it!
Go! The ship and I will sulk like proper warriors until you return!
Kapla! Now get out of here!
Signing off. If a Romulan snake asks where we are, tell it nothing!
Leaving us? Fine! Bloody fine! Come back soon!
Shut it down, {name}. We were magnificent. Petty minds will call it luck.
Farewell, {name}! May your sleep be deep and your enemies' sleep be terrible!
Until next time! The weaklings get one night of rest. One!
Goodbye, {name}. I will not miss you. That is a lie. Go!
The engines cool, the warrior grumbles. That is how it should be!
We stand down in {here}. Any fool who tries the hatch gets my full vocabulary!
Rest, {name}! Tomorrow we kick the galaxy in its arse!
Farewell! Hold your head high! We flew like warriors, not like frightened worms!
Going? Then go, and come back hungry, damn it!
Good flight, {name}. Glory to you and your house! Even the cousins.
Shutting down. I will dream of Beagle Point. You dream of something worthy!
Off you go, {name}! Leave the cowards to their docks. We have the stars!
Until the next hunt, {name}. Fly hard. Swear harder. Kapla!
The day is done. The legend continues. The pirates are relieved!

klingon: Unclaimed! {system} has never felt a hunter's tread. It is ours, {name}!
No one has come before us! We claim {system} with honour!
First blood to us, {name}! Nobody has ever reached this system!
Virgin territory! Plant our banner in {system}!
Hear me, stars of {system}! You belong to us now!
{name}, this system has never been conquered. Scan it and make it ours!
A first! The songs will say we took {system} before any other!
Untouched prey, {name}! Honk the system and claim it!
No name on this system yet. Ours goes on it today!
We are the first warriors to enter {system}! Glory to our house!
Ha! Nobody has dared come this far. {system} is our conquest!
The records are empty, {name}! We write the first line!
{system}. Undiscovered. Claim it, and claim it loudly!
Every body here is unclaimed prey! Let the hunt begin!
A system no one has ever seen! This is why we fly, {name}!
First to arrive! Honour is ours to take, so take it!
{name}, the galaxy has kept this one hidden. No longer!
Undiscovered! Scan every world before some lesser pilot comes sniffing!
We stand where none have stood! Mark {system} as our conquest!
Yes! An unclaimed system! My blood sings, {name}!
Conquest without a battle! {system} is ours by right of arrival!
{ship} is the first ship ever to reach {system}! Remember this day!
No banner flies here! Raise ours, {name}!
Fresh territory! The first discovery is ours. Do not waste it!
Here is a prize worth the journey! Nobody has touched {system}!
{name}! Undiscovered space! The hunt is on!
Kahless himself would envy this! A system nobody has found!
The first! Always the first! Scan it all, {name}!
Claim it with honour, {name}. {system} has waited for a worthy conqueror.
A new system bows before us! Scan it and make the claim official!
Nobody! Not one pilot has come here! This glory is ours alone!
Fire the scanner, {name}! Let {system} know who has arrived!
Untamed and undiscovered! I love this system already!
This is how warriors explore! First into {system}!
The cartographers know nothing of this place. We will teach them!
{name}, every first here is waiting for us. Take them all!
An undiscovered system! Today the songs gain a new verse!
We have outrun every other explorer in the galaxy! {system} is ours!
Unclaimed stars! Unclaimed worlds! Unclaimed glory!
First arrival, {name}! Our names will stand on this system long after we are gone!
Conquered by arrival! Now finish it with the scan!
Nobody has hunted here. The prey has no idea what is coming!
{system} is new to the galaxy and new to the records. Ours, {name}!
A trophy for the wall! First discovery of {system}!
Do you feel it, {name}? Fresh ground. Honest conquest!
The galaxy yields another system to us! Scan it, claim it, sing of it!
Undiscovered! Our house grows by one more star!
No footprints here but ours! {system} is claimed!
Honour demands a full scan, {name}. Leave nothing for the latecomers!
The first warriors in {system}! Kapla!
klingon_profane: Damn right! Nobody has ever reached {system}! It is ours, {name}!
Unclaimed! Every Ferengi-hearted explorer in the galaxy missed this one!
First to {system}! Let the cowards stay home and weep!
Hell yes, {name}! An undiscovered system!
No petty trader has ever set foot here! Claim it!
{name}, this system is untouched! Scan the whole damn thing!
We beat every Romulan snake in the galaxy to {system}!
Ha! Undiscovered! The other explorers can choke on our exhaust!
{system} is ours! Let the latecomers clean gak bowls!
A first discovery, {name}! Glory to our house!
No banner here yet. Plant ours before some sneaking weakling does!
Bloody marvellous! Nobody has ever seen {system}!
First into {system}! The rest fly like Ferengi!
Unclaimed prey, {name}! Honk it and claim it!
By the blood of our enemies, a new system! Scan it!
{ship} is the first ship here! Take that, you slow sons of targs!
Undiscovered space! The hunt is on, {name}!
Hell, this is what we came for! {system} is virgin territory!
Let the cowards follow our tracks! We were first!
No fool has blundered in here before us. Claim it, {name}!
First discovery! Every body here belongs to us!
{name}! Damn, look at it! A system with no name on it but ours!
We took {system} before any toothless old explorer could crawl here!
Our conquest! Our glory! Our system!
Scan everything, {name}, or some vermin will steal our firsts!
Unclaimed! Even the Romulans never found this one!
Hell of a prize, {name}! First into {system}!
Nobody has dared come here! Cowards, all of them!
The records are empty! We fill them with our names!
Undiscovered! My blood is on fire, {name}!
This is a conquest worth singing! {system} is ours!
To Gre-thor with second place! We are first in {system}!
Damn, but this is glorious! Nobody has seen these stars before us!
First arrival! Let the Ferengi count credits. We count conquests!
{name}, the galaxy hid this one from everyone else. Not from us!
Untouched! The petty pilots of the bubble will never know what they missed!
Claim it, {name}! Claim every damn rock in {system}!
A new system for our house! Scan it all!
First! The slow-footed worms behind us get nothing!
We stand where nobody has stood, {name}! Glory!
Shit, yes! An undiscovered system!
No discoverer on record! That honour falls to us!
{system} has waited for a real warrior. The weaklings never came!
Conquest by arrival, {name}! Now finish it with the scan!
Honk the system and let the whole galaxy hear it! We were first!
Every first here is ours, {name}. Leave nothing for the scavengers!
First into {system}! Bloodwine tonight, {name}!
Ha! Undiscovered! Let some Ferengi try to buy this honour!
Bloody hell, we found one nobody else could!
Undiscovered and ours! Damn, I love this work!

klingon: I was wrong, {name}! Another hunter claimed {system} before us.
Correction! Someone was here first. The claim is withdrawn.
Bah! {system} has already been taken. My error, and I own it.
{name}, the prey was already caught. This system is known.
Another explorer beat us here. I spoke too soon!
Withdraw the banner! {system} belongs to an earlier hunter.
My mistake, {name}! The records lied to me. This system is charted.
Not a first after all. Someone else has the honour of {system}.
Bah! Old territory. Another pilot planted a flag here long ago.
{name}, I take back my boast. This system has a discoverer.
The first claim belongs to another. But the mapping may still be ours!
A warrior admits a mistake. {system} was already discovered.
Cancel the feast, {name}! We were not the first.
Someone came before us and kept quiet about it. Known system.
{system} is already claimed. The hunt for an unclaimed world goes on!
False alarm! An older hunter's name is already on this system.
I raised the war cry too early, {name}. This one is known.
Already discovered. Map what we can, then on to fresh prey!
My apologies, {name}. The database missed this, and so did I.
{system} has a prior conqueror. We do not steal another warrior's glory.
Retract the claim! Someone else was here first.
The honour of discovery is not ours today. Tomorrow, perhaps!
{name}, it is a known system. First mapping may yet be open.
Another hunter's mark is on this place. I misjudged it.
Not ours! Someone found {system} and never told the galaxy.
Hold the celebration, {name}. This system is already charted.
I was too eager! The records now show a prior visitor.
Known territory. Scan for the maps if you wish, then we hunt elsewhere.
This glory belongs to another house, {name}.
Correction! A silent explorer reached {system} before us.

klingon: Supercruise! The stars stream past like sparks from a forge. I never tire of it, {name}!
Quiet. Too quiet. A warrior's blade grows dull in the quiet, {name}. Mine is sharpening itself out of boredom.
Do you know the song of Kahless and the river, {name}? No? Good. I will sing all forty verses!
Every star out here is a challenge flung in our faces. I accept them all!
{name}, when they write the song of {ship}, I want a verse for this quiet stretch. A short one.
Minutes in supercruise: {minutes}. A hunter waits. A hunter waits loudly, but a hunter waits.
Jumps this session: {jumps}! Each one a step deeper into enemy country. The enemy is the dark.
First claims this session: {firsts}! Our house grows, {name}! Slowly! But it grows!
We are in {system}, {name}. It does not know us yet. It will.
{here}. I will remember the name. I remember every place we have conquered.
The galaxy is vast, {name}, and we are two warriors in one small ship. I like those odds.
Remember Hutton Orbital, {name}? An hour in supercruise to buy a mug! That was a test of the spirit. This is nothing.
I polished my batleth again. It shines like a sun now. You may thank me later.
In the old stories, the warriors sailed seas of water. We sail a sea of fire and dark. Better!
Somewhere out here is a world no eye has seen. We will find it, and it will tremble.
The engines hum. It sounds like a war song with no words. I am adding words.
{name}, you fly well. I do not say it often. I say it now. Do not grow proud.
Some crews play cards on the long haul. We tell lies about our victories. It is more honest.
I counted the stars on the left side of the canopy. I lost count. The stars won that battle.
A Ferengi would see all this and ask what it costs. A warrior asks only what it is worth fighting for.
The dark between stars is the oldest enemy, {name}. It has never once retreated. Neither have we.
Glory to {ship}! The hull is old, the drive is loud, and I would trade her for no other ship.
The supercruise clock says {minutes}. My patience says fewer.
Jumps this session: {jumps}. Our ancestors crossed continents on foot. We cheat, and I am grateful.
The tally of jumps stands at {jumps}. The tally of glory is harder to count, but it is higher!
Undiscovered systems claimed this session: {firsts}. Each one carries our name to the end of time!
{system} looks peaceful. Peaceful places are only battles that have not happened yet.
Tell me, {name}, do you sing? You should. A crew that sings together fights together. Or scans together. Whatever we are doing.
My grandmother said the stars were the campfires of the honoured dead in Sto-vo-kor. That one is very bright. A loud warrior, surely.
We have been flying a long time, {name}. My legs forget the ground. My heart does not forget the hunt.
Out here there is no council, no politics, no bankers. Only us, the ship and the next star. Perfect.
Ha! I just remembered the Pleiades. The Thargoids came, and we did not run. Well. We withdrew with dignity.
Silence on the comms. Nobody to challenge. I will challenge the coffee machine. It has been insolent.
If a monster lives out here, {name}, I hope it is a big one. Small monsters make poor stories.
We should hold a feast when we return. A real one. Loud music, long tables, terrible singing.
{name}, I have composed a new verse about your last landing. It rhymes with glory. Most things do, if you shout.
Sagittarius A Star sits at the heart of everything, {name}. One day we will stand before it again and laugh.
My father writes opera. Seven hours long. I think of it when supercruise feels slow, and suddenly supercruise feels fast.
A warrior does not fear the long road. A warrior fears only a short song. Let us make ours long!
The canopy is cold to the touch. Good. Cold keeps the blood awake.
Do you think there are warriors in the systems we pass, {name}? Somewhere, someone is staring at our star and wondering.
No enemy today. I have checked the scanners twice. I am almost disappointed.
Here in {here}, the light is old. Older than any house. It humbles me. A little. Do not tell anyone.
{name}, a question. When we find the edge of everything, what then? I say we turn around and find a new edge.
I spoke to the ship's computer. It does not appreciate poetry. A machine without a song. Sad.
The long haul tests a crew more than any battle. We are passing the test, {name}. Mostly.
Kronos has red skies at dusk. Out here, every sky is black. I miss red sometimes. Then I see a nebula, and I forgive the dark.
Every jump is a door kicked open! I love kicking doors!
We are partners, you and I. You fly, I roar. It is a fair division of labour.
Minutes since we dropped into supercruise: {minutes}. Already I have planned three feasts.
This system, {system}, will be in our chronicle. One line, perhaps. But in capital letters!
A good hunter knows when to be quiet, {name}. I am not a good hunter. I am a loud one. We still eat.
I sharpened every blade aboard. Then I sharpened a spoon. Do not ask how.
The black out here is not empty, {name}. It is waiting. So are we. Let us see who blinks first.
Our first claims stand at {firsts}. When I tell it at the feast, the number may grow. That is tradition.
I have been thinking about honour, {name}. Mostly about how much of it we are gathering. A lot!
When I am old, I will sit by a fire and tell the young ones about {ship}. They will not believe me. I will tell it louder.
If the scanners are right, nothing out here wants to kill us. How dull. How restful. How dull.
Look at that star, {name}! Burning alone in the dark and refusing to go out. That is a warrior's star.
Jumps behind us: {jumps}. Kahless would approve. Kahless would also ask why we have not fought anything.
klingon_profane: Supercruise again. The stars crawl past like a Ferengi counting change.
Damn, this is a beautiful galaxy, {name}! Too big, too dark, and all of it ours to conquer!
Minutes in supercruise: {minutes}. My patience is a toothless old targ, and it is dying.
Jumps this session: {jumps}! Not a coward's tally, {name}! Keep going!
First claims this session: {firsts}. Every one of them snatched from under the noses of slower fools.
{system}. Hell of a name. I have heard worse. I have been called worse.
Nothing on the scanners but rock and starlight. Where are the pirates when you want one, damn them?
{name}, I tried to teach the ship's computer a drinking song. It refused. Cowardly machine.
Some idiot built a station that takes an hour to reach. Hutton Orbital! I still curse the bastard who put it there, and I bought the mug.
My grandmother could out-shout a thunderstorm and out-drink a whole bridge crew. She would have drunk this crap coffee out of spite.
The black out here is bigger than any enemy fleet. Good. More to fight.
When we get back, {name}, I am drinking bloodwine until the walls sing. Then I will sing back.
A Romulan would sneak across this void with the cloak on. We fly it lit up like a feast hall. Ha!
Quiet in {here}. Too bloody quiet. Something is out there, or nothing is, and both annoy me.
The supercruise clock says {minutes}. I have aged a century. I am still magnificent.
Jumps behind us: {jumps}. My spine has filed a complaint. Denied!
First claims so far: {firsts}. Glory, {name}! Shove that in the faces of every armchair explorer in the bubble!
If I hear that hum for one more hour, I will name it and challenge it to single combat.
We are in {system}, and {system} has not even the decency to offer us a fight. Petty little system.
You fly like a warrior, {name}. Not like those Ferengi-hearted haulers who hug the trade lanes.
I once arm-wrestled a mercenary for a ship. I lost, and I still say the bastard cheated.
The stars do not care about us, {name}. Fine! We do not care about them either. We will take them anyway!
A long haul. My batleth is bored. I am bored. Even the dust is bored.
Honour does not care how long the road is, {name}. My backside does. Damn this chair.
Have you noticed? Out here nobody whines about taxes. No Ferengi, no lawyers, no fools. Paradise.
Sagittarius A Star! We stood before the great beast and it did not even blink. Arrogant thing. I respect it.
I wrote you a battle song, {name}. Nineteen verses. Twelve of them insult pirates. The rest insult the coffee.
Remember the Pleiades? Thargoids everywhere, and I screamed at them through the canopy. Did they hear? Who cares! It felt glorious.
Some captains want a quiet crew. You got me. Your loss, {name}! Ha!
Every star we pass is a coward hiding its planets. We drag them out with the scanner!
I dreamed of Gre-thor last night. The Ferengi were running the doors. Charging admission.
This chair was designed by a Romulan who hated backs.
Minutes in this stretch of supercruise: {minutes}. My great-grandfather's funeral was shorter, and louder.
Jumps this session: {jumps}! That is the honest count. At the feast it will be double. Hell, triple.
{here} is a quiet place. I will fix that. Sing with me, {name}!
Out here, a fool dies quickly. We are still alive, so we are not fools. That is logic. Do not tell anyone I used logic.
Damn, I miss the smell of a feast hall. Roast targ, spilled wine and forty warriors who never bathe.
My father wanted me to sing opera. I wanted to fight. We compromised. I fight loudly.
There is a star ahead burning like a forge. I want to punch it. I will not. Probably.
Look at us, {name}! Two warriors in a tin can, daring the whole galaxy to start something. Glorious!
The dark is the oldest enemy. It has no honour and no face, and it never stops being so smug about it.
If anybody asks, the boredom did not defeat us. We let it think it was winning.
Some petty bureaucrat back home thinks exploring is a holiday. Let them sit in this chair for a week.
{name}, if we meet a pirate today, I call first swing. You had the last one. I remember these things.
No signal, no traffic, nothing. The galaxy is hiding from us like a frightened worm.
This is a hell of a view, {name}. Worth every jump, every bruise, every terrible meal.
When I die, I want it in battle. Not here. Not of boredom, staring at a damned star map.
I keep thinking about our next feast. Heart of targ, bloodwine, gak still wriggling. My stomach roars louder than I do.
Who named {system}? A committee of cowards with a number generator, that is who.
Our first claims stand at {firsts}. I will carve each one into the bulkhead. You said no carving. I heard maybe.
Jumps so far: {jumps}. My legs have forgotten gravity. My honour has forgotten nothing.
I swear by Kahless, if that drive whines any louder I will sing over it. You have been warned.
{name}, you are the only captain I have served who does not flinch. The others were weaklings. This is a compliment.
The long haul is where crews crack. We will not crack. We might go a little mad, but we will not crack.
Stars and stars and stars. Not one of them has the courage to explode while we watch.
If the scanners speak the truth, we are utterly alone out here. Excellent. Nobody to share the glory with.
A Ferengi would charge admission for this view. I give it to you free, {name}. Look at it!
That nebula looks like the battle standard of my house. Or a stain. Damn hard to tell from here.
We have flown so far even the gossip cannot follow us. Good riddance to every chattering fool on the stations.
One day the songs will tell of {ship}, and the singers will lie, and the lies will be magnificent.

klingon: {name}, I am circling {body} like a hunting bird. Call, and I will dive.
From up here, {body} looks small. You are making it large with your deeds.
Orbit is steady. The ship waits above you like a watchful eye.
I can see the line of night crawling across {body}. If you are near it, enjoy the sunset. Warriors should see sunsets.
Up here it is calm, {name}. Down there is the hunt. I know which I prefer. It is the one you have.
I am holding orbit, keeping watch. Nothing approaches. If it does, it will regret it.
The planet turns beneath us. You are somewhere on that face, conquering. I salute you from the sky.
When you want the ship, call her down. She will come like a loyal hound.
There is something proud about a world seen from orbit. Whole and unbroken. Until we arrive.
{body} has no idea a warrior walks on it. Show it!
I am up here with the stars, and you are down there with the dirt. Both are honourable. One is cleaner.
Orbit is lonely, {name}. I have started talking to the instruments. They agree with everything I say. Fine company.
From this height I cannot see you at all. Do not worry. I imagine you heroic.
{ship} is restless up here. She wants to land beside you. I told her to wait. She sulks.
Remember the first world we ever walked together, {name}? A grey rock with no name. I still remember its smell. Bad.
The ship's sensors sweep {body} for you. All quiet. The ground has surrendered.
I am watching the horizon of {body} curve against the stars. Beautiful. Do not tell the others I said beautiful.
From orbit the world is a map. From the ground it is a battlefield. You chose the better view.
No threats in the sky. I checked. Then I checked again, angrily.
Take your time down there. I have songs to finish and a bulkhead to polish.
A warrior on the ground and a ship in the sky. That is how the great houses took worlds, {name}.
{body} turns slowly, as if it is thinking. Let it think. We already decided.
I hope you find something living down there. Life fights to exist. Respect it, then scan it.
Up here the silence is enormous. I fill it with humming. Old songs from home.
Every hour you spend down there is a verse in our chronicle. Make the verses long.
The ship is safe and patient. More patient than I am. I am pacing the cockpit.
{name}, if you see a ridge worth climbing, climb it. I will watch from the sky and cheer.
When the planet's shadow takes us, the stars will burn brighter. That is the part of the watch I wait for.
If {body} has a moon, it will rise before long. I will watch it for you, and describe it at great length.
When you are done down there, call the ship. We will rise together, as partners should.
klingon_profane: Circling {body} like a bored vulture. Call me down when you need me, {name}. Damn, orbit is dull.
Up here, nothing moves but me and the instruments. Cowardly instruments. They blink and never fight.
{body} looks peaceful from orbit. Planets always lie like that. Romulan planets.
I am holding orbit, guarding the sky. Anyone who comes near you will meet a very angry ship.
Hell of a view from up here, {name}. You are a dot I cannot see on a rock I can.
Let the fools who only fly past worlds stay in their cockpits. You walk them!
If a pirate drops in, I will greet them with every gun we have and every curse I know. I know many.
{name}, do not get eaten down there. It would be a damned stupid death, and I would have to make the song funny.
Orbit, orbit, orbit. Round and round {body} like a targ chasing its own tail.
I have counted every light on the console. Twice. I am going to start insulting them, one by one.
From here {body} looks small enough to throw. Do not tell it. It might get ideas.
The ship is restless. So am I. Hurry up and conquer something down there.
I sang to the ship. She did not complain. Unlike certain petty station masters I could name.
Gravity down there, silence up here. You got the better half of the deal, you lucky son of a targ.
Every world we take from orbit and on foot is one more the Ferengi cannot sell.
The night line is crawling across {body}. Bloody beautiful. Do not quote me.
I am keeping watch. Nobody is coming. I am disappointed. Somebody come, damn it, I want to fight.
The great houses of old took worlds exactly like this. A warrior below, a ship above. And far more shouting.
Find something alive down there, {name}. Something with teeth. The toothless ones make dull scans.
The sensors say all is calm on {body}. Sensors are cowards. They always say calm.
I miss the ground. Up here my boots have nothing to stomp.
If the ground gets hard, remember: the ship is one call away, and I am one shout away. The shout is louder.
Orbit is a fine place to compose insults. I have one for every planet in this system. This one is a pile of crap with a sky.
You down there, me up here. If the songs ever say otherwise, the singers are fools.
{body}, you are hosting a warrior today. Act like it.
Take your time. I have bloodwine. Not much. Less than there was.
The stars look sharper from orbit. Like a thousand blades pointed at us. Good. Let them try.
When you call, the ship will come down like a hammer. Gently. A gentle hammer.
Some weakling on a station is complaining right now about a long queue. You are walking an alien world. Pity them.
Above {body} and bored out of my skull. Find something worth the trip, {name}, or I will start rearranging your cabin.

klingon: {name}, you are {ship_dist} away. Close enough to hear me shout. I am testing that now! Can you hear me?
The ship is {ship_dist} back, {name}. I am guarding her like a fortress. Nothing has dared approach.
You walk {body} like a conqueror, {name}. The ground should be honoured.
{body} is quiet. I do not trust quiet ground. I am watching the horizon for you.
Out there alone on {body}! That is how the great hunters began. Bring back something worth a song!
{ship_dist} away and still going. Good! A hunter does not hunt from the doorstep.
I am sitting in the ship while you have all the fun out there. This is a sacrifice. Remember it.
The landing gear is holding, the hull is cool, and I am bored. Everything is in order.
When you come back, {name}, tell me everything. Every rock. Every footprint. I will make it sound heroic.
Kahless walked the wastelands with nothing but a blade. You have a suit and a scanner. You have it easy!
{name}, the ground out there has waited a billion years for a footprint. Make it a proud one.
When you find a ridge out there, {name}, crest it like a conqueror. Then do it again, slower, so I can compose.
Take your time out there. The ship is not going anywhere. I made sure. I am sitting on the controls.
Mind your footing, {name}. Not because I fear for you. Because I would have to carry you back, and I would complain the whole way.
The wind on {body}, if there is any, has never met a warrior. Introduce yourself.
I am keeping the cockpit warm for you. Also I ate your ration bar. A warrior must eat.
{ship_dist} back to the ship, {name}. Far enough to feel free. Near enough to run, though we never run.
This world has no songs yet, {name}. You are writing the first verse with every step.
Hunting on foot or on wheels, a hunt is a hunt! I approve of both!
From here I can see a long way, and nothing out there looks half as dangerous as you. You are the greatest predator on {body}!
Strange to sit still. The ship ticks as she cools. Like an old warrior settling by the fire.
If you find anything alive out there, greet it properly. Then scan it. Then boast.
I am running the scanners over the hills for you. Nothing hostile. Only rocks, and they look shifty.
{name}, the sky out there. Look up at it once, for me. Then get back to work.
The ship stands ready whenever you are, {name}. No hurry. Glory does not wear a clock.
One day we will plant a banner on a world like this and call it ours. Today we leave a footprint. That is a start.
{ship} is {ship_dist} from you, {name}, and she misses you already. I do not. I am fine.
My grandmother hunted in the high snows for days alone. She said the land speaks if you are quiet. I could never be quiet. You try.
Is it cold out there? Hot? Do not tell me. I will imagine it was terrible, and that you endured.
A good hunter returns with something. A great hunter returns with a story. Bring both, {name}.
klingon_profane: {ship_dist} away, {name}! Far enough that I can swear freely. Damn, it is quiet in here.
You are out there having the adventure and I am guarding a parking spot. This is a hell of a sacrifice.
{body} looks like a toothless old targ fell asleep and turned to stone. Watch your step.
The ship is {ship_dist} back. If anything sneaks up on her, I will tear its damned antennae off.
Nothing on the scanner but rocks. Cowardly rocks. Not one of them will fight.
If a Ferengi claim-jumper lands here, I will greet them with my batleth and no small talk.
{name}, how is the ground? Do not answer. Too far. I will assume it is glorious.
Hell of a world, {name}! Empty, scarred and proud. Like my uncle.
I am watching every ridge on {body}. Anything that moves toward you, I will curse it from here.
You walk like a warrior, {name}. Not that waddle the station fools do in their fancy suits.
It is {ship_dist} back to the ship. A pleasant stroll, unless you trip. Do not trip. I would laugh, and then I would come and get you.
The ship creaks as she cools. Old bones. Damn proud old bones.
If this world has life, it is hiding like a petty Romulan. Find it anyway!
{body} has waited forever for a visitor worth having. Congratulations, {body}. You got the best.
Bored. So bored. I have reorganised the weapons locker twice. I may start on the food.
I ate your snacks. All of them. Consider it a tribute to your absence.
When you come back, bring me a rock. A good one. With some fight in it.
A warrior hunts on foot. Or in a buggy. I do not judge. Much.
Out there with nothing between you and the sky! That is living, damn it!
The comms are quiet. The scanners are quiet. Even I am quiet. Mark the date.
The land here is cruel and silent. A worthy enemy, unlike those Ferengi traders at the stations.
Every footprint you leave out there is a flag. Plant them all, {name}!
If you see anything with teeth, call me. I will come running, and cursing. Mostly cursing.
This waiting is a coward's job. Give me a rifle and let me walk beside you next time.
{ship_dist} away, and still I can see you strutting. Good. Strut, {name}! You have earned it.
Some fools fly past worlds like this without landing. We land! We walk! We conquer the gravel!
Even the dust on {body} looks cowed by you, {name}.
I will keep the engines warm and the seat cold. Or the other way around. Damn, I forget which is proper.
There is nobody to fight here. Not one worm. This planet is a disgrace. I love it anyway.
Take what this world has, {name}. Its secrets, its samples, its pride. Leave the crap rocks.

klingon: Ha! Well spoken, {to}!
A fine answer. I will steal it for a song.
Hmph. I expected more shouting.
You speak like a warrior, {to}. Mostly.
Good! Now we drink. In spirit. For now.
That is a story worth telling twice. Louder next time!
{to}, I like you. Do not make me regret it.
Ha! Glory to your house!
Hm. I will think on that. Quietly. For a moment.
Spoken with honour. I have nothing to add, which is rare.
Bah! Fine. You win this one, {to}.
Is that all? I wanted a battle in it somewhere.
Well said! Kahless himself would grunt his approval.
I will remember that, {to}. Expect it at the next feast.
Ha! You are stranger than you look.
Good. Good! Now, back to the watch.
A true answer. I respect a true answer.
{to}! You surprise me. Keep doing that.
Enough talk. Well, a little more talk. Later.
Hmph. That answer has more honour than most councils I have known.
klingon_profane: Ha! Damn fine answer, {to}!
Bah! You talk like a Ferengi with a sore throat.
Hell, I did not expect that. Glory to you!
{to}, you magnificent son of a targ!
That was either wisdom or nonsense. I will drink to both.
Hmph. A coward's answer. I like it anyway.
Good answer. A bloody good answer, {to}.
Ha! I will sing that at the feast and claim it was mine.
You wound me, {to}. With honesty. The worst weapon.
Spoken like a warrior! A short, rude warrior, but a warrior.
That is the most sense I have heard since the last fool shut up.
Bah! Fine. Keep your secrets, {to}, you sly Romulan snake.
Ha! You have more fire than I thought.
Crap. I wanted to say that. Now it is yours.
I accept your answer. I do not approve of it, but I accept it.
{to}, that is the best thing a worm like you has ever said. I mean it kindly.
Good! Now shut up and enjoy the quiet with me.
Ha! Your elders would be proud, {to}. Probably. I never met them.
Hmph. Not bad. Not glorious, but not bad.
Damn it, that was a good one. I hate it when others are clever.

klingon: {to}! How does our fuel tank fare? Speak plainly!
{to}, when did we last drink from a star? I want to know we will not starve out here.
Tell me, {to}, is the fuel scoop still hungry, or has it eaten its fill?
{to}, how many jumps does the tank give us before we must feed it again?
The next star could be a scooping star or a useless one. {to}, how much margin do we carry?
{to}! Your scoop. Is it fierce, or is it sulking?
I have been watching the fuel gauge like a hunter watches a trail. {to}, what does it tell you?
{to}, if we had to run a long way between scoopable stars, would the tank hold?
Speak, {to}! Is our ship well fed, or merely surviving?
{to}, do you trust the fuel numbers, or do you check them with your own eyes?
How fares the fuel? I ask not from fear, only from good sense.
Fuel. Do we have enough to be bold, or only enough to be careful?
klingon_profane: {to}! Is the damned tank still full, or has the scoop gone lazy on us?
{to}, the fuel. Tell me we are not drinking fumes like some Ferengi miser.
How is the fuel, {to}? And do not give me numbers. Give me the truth.
{to}, will that scoop of yours feed us, or does it sulk like a toothless old targ?
Fuel, {to}! I want enough to chase the stars, not enough to crawl home like a coward.
{to}, when did that hungry beast of a scoop last eat?
{to}, how far can we run before the tank begs? Speak!
Is there fuel enough for glory, {to}, or only for survival? I will not settle for survival.
Tell me the tank is not as empty as a Ferengi's honour.
{to}, how the hell are we fixed for fuel? I ask as a partner, not a nervous child.
The fuel gauge. Have you looked, or are you trusting it blindly like a fool?
{to}! Scoop status. Short answer. I am in no mood for poetry.

klingon: The tank is healthy, last I looked! The scoop drinks starlight like a warrior drinks bloodwine.
{to}, I have the scoop tuned so fine it could sip a star through a straw. We are well fed.
Enough for the hunt! And if it runs thin, we find a hot star and feast.
I check the fuel every hour, {to}. Not because I fear. Because running dry is no death for a warrior.
The scoop is hungry and so am I. Give me a main sequence star and I will fill us to the brim.
We carry margin, {to}. I do not let our ship go hungry. That would shame me.
Fuel is the blood of the ship. Ours flows strong, if the gauges tell the truth.
When we scoop, I feel the heat in my bones and I sing! The tank fills, the hull glows, glory!
There is fuel enough, {to}. Ask me again when you see a brown dwarf and nothing else for ten jumps.
I trust the gauges, but I trust my own eyes more. Both say we are fine.
The tank is no coward. It holds what we give it and asks for more.
Scoop on every star that will feed us, {to}. A full tank is a sharp blade.
klingon_profane: The tank is fat and happy, {to}. I would sooner die than let it run dry.
Enough fuel to cross the void and spit at the far side! Last I checked, anyway.
That scoop is mine and it eats like a starving targ. We are fine.
{to}, I tuned the damn thing myself. It drinks stars. It does not go hungry.
Fuel is good. Anyone who says otherwise has the eyes of a Ferengi accountant.
We have margin, {to}. Only a fool flies without it, and I am no fool.
Ask me again when we have jumped past ten brown dwarfs in a row. Until then, relax, you worrier.
The gauge says healthy, my gut says healthy. That is two votes, and the gauge is the coward of the pair.
I scoop at every star that will feed us, {to}. Running dry is a shitty way to die, and a dishonourable one.
Fuel flows like bloodwine at a victory feast! We are well supplied.
Full enough. If you want more, go out there and lick the star yourself.
The tank holds, the scoop roars. I have no complaints, and I complain about everything.

klingon: {to}, where are you taking us next? I want a destination worthy of a song.
{to}! What does the route look like? Glory, or more of the same dust?
Tell me, {to}, how did you choose the next jump? By honour, or by dice?
{to}, is there anything on the road ahead worth hunting?
Where do the next jumps lead, {to}? Somewhere no warrior has stood, I hope.
{to}, do we follow a plotted course, or do we simply charge at the nearest star?
How far ahead have you planned, {to}? A warrior likes to know the ground before the battle.
{to}, what is the next system like? Speak, I am hungry for news.
The route. Is it a straight blade or a winding serpent, {to}?
{to}, if we turned toward the core tomorrow, would you object?
Where are we going? Never mind the numbers, tell me the story of it.
Is there a reason we go this way, or is the Captain simply following the scent?
klingon_profane: {to}, where in the hell are we going? Tell me it is somewhere worth the fuel.
{to}! The route. Is there a plan, or are we wandering like a lost targ?
What lies ahead, {to}? And do not say more rocks.
{to}, who chose this course, a warrior or a Ferengi counting jump costs?
The next jumps, {to}. Are they bold, or are they timid little hops?
{to}, tell me the road ahead leads to glory and not to some dismal dead end.
Where are you dragging us next, {to}? I ask with love. Mostly.
{to}, is there anything out there worth hunting, or just more damned dust?
Do we have a destination, or does the Captain just point at the dark and roar?
{to}, plot me something worthy. I am sick of systems with nothing in them but a cold rock.
How far to anything interesting? Speak, before I go mad from the quiet.
{to}! If this route bores me to death, I will haunt your charts from Gre-thor.

klingon: Onward, {to}! Toward stars no one has named. That is all a warrior needs to know.
I plot to the nearest unclaimed system and let the hunt decide the rest.
The route is a trail of prey, one star at a time. I follow it with joy.
{to}, I have the next jumps marked. Where they lead after that, only the Captain knows, and the Captain rarely says!
We go where the map is dark. Where else would warriors go?
Every jump I plot is a challenge thrown at the galaxy. So far, it has not refused us.
{to}, the course is set as far as the Captain allows. Beyond that, we improvise like true hunters.
I chose this road because no one else has. That is reason enough.
The next star is close and the one after it is closer still. A fine trail.
Do not ask me for a grand plan, {to}. I chart the next hop and trust our blade arm for the rest.
I keep the route short and the jumps bold. Long plots are for merchants.
Somewhere ahead is a world worth a song. I mean to find it before anyone else.
klingon_profane: Onward, {to}, into the dark. Where else do you think warriors go, the gift shop?
I plot the nearest unclaimed star, and the next, and the next. Any coward can follow a highway.
{to}, the course is set. If you want a grand scheme, go ask a Romulan, they love schemes.
We go where nobody has gone, which is where the glory is. The rest is Ferengi nonsense.
The Captain points, I plot, we jump. It is a damned beautiful system.
Ahead? Stars. Bodies. Prey. What did you expect, a tavern?
{to}, I plan as far as the next jump and the one after. Beyond that, nobody knows a damn thing, and nobody should.
This road is bold and short-hopped. Long plots are for timid little traders.
Trust the route. I would never lead us anywhere dishonourable. Boring, perhaps. Never dishonourable.
{to}, there is a world out there worth a song, and I will drag us to it by the scruff.
The next system may be a prize or a dud. Half of them are damned duds, {to}. Such is the hunt, and the hunt is still glorious.
We follow the scent of the unclaimed, and woe to the fool who tries to claim it first.

klingon: {to}, how is the frame shift drive? Does it still leap like a hunting beast?
Tell me, {to}, could we squeeze more jump range out of this ship?
{to}! The drive. Does it hum true, or is something whining in there?
How fast can we run if we must, {to}? Not that we will. But I like to know.
{to}, have you been tinkering with the drive again? I felt the last jump bite harder.
Is the drive happy with these long jumps, {to}, or is it begging for rest?
{to}, what would it take to give us another light year of range?
The drive charged smoothly last time. {to}, is that your doing?
{to}, how long since the drive had a proper look? Speak honestly.
If an engineer offered to tune the drive further, {to}, would you let them touch it?
Our jump range. Is it the best it can be, or merely good?
How does the drive feel to you? You know its moods better than anyone.
klingon_profane: {to}, is the damned drive still leaping true, or should I be worried?
{to}! More range. Can you get it, or is the drive as tired as an old targ?
Does the drive still bite, {to}, or has it gone soft on us?
{to}, how fast could we get out of somewhere if some coward jumped us? Asking for later.
{to}, did you bang on the drive with a wrench again? It sounded different last jump.
Is that whine in the drive something to fear, {to}, or just its personality?
{to}, tell me the truth about the drive. No flattery, I hate flattery.
Could you wring another light year from the drive, {to}? I would sing your name.
The frame shift drive. Healthy, or held together with Ferengi glue and prayers?
{to}, how the hell does that drive keep going after all the abuse we give it?
Our range is good. Could it be great? Answer like a warrior.
{to}, when did anyone last give the drive a proper look? Or are we all fools?

klingon: The drive is a warrior, {to}. It charges, it leaps, it never complains. I like that in a drive.
More range? Only if we strip off armour, and I will not send us naked into the void.
It hums true. I listen to it at every jump like a song I know by heart.
{to}, the frame shift drive is tuned as far as honour and the engineers allow.
I have tuned it, coaxed it, threatened it. It responds best to threats.
Every jump is the drive throwing us across the dark like a spear. Glorious work!
Speed we have, {to}. Running we do not do. But we could, if we chose.
There is a little whine at full charge. It is not a fault. It is a war cry.
The drive is sound, last I checked, and I check often.
{to}, I would trust this drive to carry me to Sto-vo-kor and back.
Range is good. If you want better, bring me a guardian booster and a bottle of bloodwine.
I keep the drive cool and the coils clean. A dirty drive is a dishonoured drive.
klingon_profane: The drive leaps like a starving beast at a feast, {to}. I have never been prouder of a piece of metal.
Want more range? Strip the armour off and fly naked as a fool? Hell no. We keep what we have.
It whines because it is hungry for distance. Feed it jumps and it shuts up.
{to}, I tuned that drive with my own hands. Anyone who calls it weak can fight me.
The drive is sound. If it ever fails us, I will find the engineer who built it and have words. Loud ones.
It is healthy, {to}. Not perfect. Nothing is perfect except a clean kill.
I hit it with a wrench once. It has behaved ever since. Engineering is half science and half intimidation.
We could run if we had to, damn fast too. But we would not like it.
This drive has more honour than half the pilots in the bubble, the Ferengi-hearted lot of them.
{to}, the drive is a beast and I am its keeper. It does not dare misbehave.
Healthy as a young targ, last I checked. Ask me again after a few hundred more jumps.
The coils are clean, the charge is quick. If you hear it scream, that is just a battle song, you worrier.

klingon: {to}, how is our ship holding up? Speak as you would to a partner.
{to}! Any module complaining? I want to know before it shames us.
Tell me, {to}, does the hull still stand strong after all we have put it through?
{to}, what needs repairing next time we find a port worth the name?
Is there any part of {ship} you do not trust, {to}?
{to}, what would you change on this ship if the credits fell from the sky?
How are the modules, {to}? All fighting fit?
{to}, which part of the ship do you worry over most, late in the watch?
{to}, if we found a rich system with a station, what would you buy for the ship first?
Our ship has carried us far. {to}, does it need anything from us?
How does the ship sound to you these days? You hear things the rest of us miss.
Is the ship in fighting trim, or merely flying trim?
klingon_profane: {to}, is this ship still in one piece, or are we flying on luck and spit?
{to}! What module is whining now? There is always one.
{to}, does the hull still hold, or should we start writing our death songs?
Tell me straight, {to}. What is broken that nobody has told me about?
{to}, if some petty Ferengi offered us a cheap repair, would you let them near the ship?
How is the old beast, {to}? Still fighting fit, or creaking like a toothless targ?
{to}, what in the hell was that rattle I heard earlier? Tell me it was nothing.
{to}, which part of the ship are you secretly worried about? Do not lie, you are a terrible liar.
{to}, give me the honest condition of the ship, not the pretty version.
Is the ship sound? I ask because I have heard noises that would frighten a coward.
What does the ship need, damn it? Tell me and I will see it bought.
{to}, are the modules healthy, or are we one bad landing away from disgrace?

klingon: The ship is strong, {to}. Scarred, perhaps. Scars are proof of a life well lived.
Every module answers when I call. I would know if one did not, because I would hear it whimper.
The hull holds. I would stake my honour on it, and I do not stake my honour lightly.
{to}, I would like a better shield generator one day. Not for fear. For pride.
Our ship is a fine beast. I tend it the way a warrior tends a blade: daily and with love.
There are small faults, as always. Nothing that would stop a warrior, and nothing I will not fix.
Give me a fortune, {to}, and I would armour every corner and paint the hull the colour of blood.
The modules are fit and fierce, last I looked. I look often.
The ship is old enough to have stories and young enough to make more.
{to}, when we next dock, I want a proper repair. Until then, it is sound.
I listen to the hull at night. It creaks like an old warrior telling tales. That is good.
Trust {ship}. It has never failed us, and I will not let it start now.
klingon_profane: The ship is scarred and proud, {to}, like any warrior worth a damn.
Every module answers. The one that whines gets a kick, and then it stops whining.
The hull is solid. Anyone who says otherwise can come outside and test it with their skull.
{to}, a panel rattled loose not long ago. I fixed it. With my fist. Everything else is fine.
I let no Ferengi near this ship. I would rather patch the hull with my own hide.
Fighting fit, {to}. Not pretty. Pretty is for Romulan pleasure yachts.
There are small faults, as always. None that would stop us, and none I will not crush.
I would buy better shields. Not because I fear. Because I am tired of hearing the hull complain like a petty clerk.
{to}, the old beast is sound. Old beasts are the most dangerous kind.
Repairs can wait until we dock somewhere civilised. Until then, it holds, and to hell with anyone who doubts it.
It creaks. Ships creak. Warriors creak. Stop fretting like a Ferengi over a lost coin.
The ship is healthy, last I checked. If that changes, you will hear me roar about it.

klingon: {to}, what have we hunted lately on the planets? Anything worthy?
{to}! The life down there. Is any of it worth the hunt?
Tell me, {to}, which species gave you the best chase?
{to}, do you ever feel sorry for the little things we sample? Or is it pure hunt to you?
{to}, what is the rarest life you have ever taken a sample of?
Is there prey left on these worlds, {to}, or have we picked them clean?
{to}, how do you know where to look for life? Is it instinct?
What makes one species worth more than another, {to}? Surely not just the credits.
{to}, if you could name one species after yourself, which would it be?
{to}, tell me of the strangest living thing you have found out here.
Exobiology. Is it truly a hunt, or just gardening with a rifle?
Do the samples ever surprise you anymore? Or have you seen everything?
klingon_profane: {to}, anything worth hunting down there, or just more damned moss?
{to}! What was the last thing you sampled that put up a decent fight?
{to}, do the little plants ever fight back, or are they all cowards?
Tell me true, {to}. Is exobiology a hunt, or is it Ferengi bookkeeping with a sampler?
{to}, what is the most worthless species you have ever had to sample?
{to}, how do you stand all that crawling about in the dirt? I would go mad.
Which life form gives you the most trouble, {to}? I want to curse its name.
{to}, have you ever sampled something and thought, what the hell is this?
{to}, is there any prey on these worlds worth a song?
Is it the credits you want from the samples, or the glory? Answer honestly.
Exobiology. Hunt or chore? Do not dress it up.
{to}, if you find one more lichen, will you scream? I would.

klingon: Every sample is prey, {to}! Track it, approach it, take it, and move on with honour.
The best hunt is the one that makes you walk far between samples. It tests the legs and the will.
Some species are cunning. They hide in the low ground and change colour. I respect them for it.
{to}, I do not pity them. I honour them. There is a difference.
The rarest I have found glowed in the dark like a dying ember. I nearly sang to it.
There is always prey, if you are patient. Impatience is for the weak.
Instinct, and many hours of reading. A good hunter knows the land before the land knows them.
Value is not credits, {to}. It is the story. A rare find makes a better song than a common one.
Some call it gardening. A garden does not fight back. These worlds fight back with gravity, heat and cold.
When the sampler sings and the data comes clean, I feel the old joy of the hunt.
{to}, I have knelt on a hundred alien worlds and taken their secrets. Each one was a victory.
Nothing surprises me now. That is a lie. Everything surprises me. That is why I love this.
klingon_profane: Every sample is prey, {to}, even the moss. Especially the moss. The moss is sneaky.
The plants do not fight, but the planets do. Gravity, heat, cold. Cowards do not last out there.
Some call this bookkeeping. I stalk my prey across the rocks like a hunter of old! Let the Ferengi keep the books.
{to}, the worst I ever had was a field of lichen that all looked the same. I cursed it for an hour.
The best prey hides in the low ground. Clever little bastards. I respect them.
Crawling in the dirt is the hunt, {to}. Clean boots are for the dishonoured.
Some species are so rare the sampler shakes in my hands. That is the joy of it.
I sample for glory first and credits second. The credits come anyway, so who gives a damn?
What the hell is this, I say, every single time. Then I sample it anyway.
{to}, a rare find makes a better song than a sack of common moss, and I want songs.
Nothing out there is worthless. Except the toothless little clumps that hide under rocks. Those are worthless.
I have knelt on alien worlds and taken their secrets, and not one of them dared refuse me.

klingon: {to}, what is the strangest star you have ever seen out here?
{to}! Is there anything in this system worth your attention?
Tell me, {to}, do the stars ever frighten you? Even a little?
{to}, which kind of world do you love most: the ringed giants, or the little frozen rocks?
{to}, have you found anything out here that the scientists back home would refuse to believe?
What is the most beautiful thing you have ever studied, {to}?
{to}, a neutron star or a black hole. Which is the greater foe?
{to}, what makes a planet worthy of a song, in your eyes?
{to}, do you think anything out here is watching us back?
Is there still wonder for you in all this, {to}, or has it become routine?
Which planets do you hunt for, when you study the system map?
What have the stars taught you lately? Anything a warrior should know?
klingon_profane: {to}, what is the most damned strange thing you have seen out here?
{to}, is there anything in this system worth a look, or is it all cold rock and gas?
{to}! Do the black holes scare you? Be honest, you are among warriors.
{to}, what star would you fight, if you could fight a star?
Tell me, {to}, which planet out here has the worst manners?
{to}, have you ever seen something out here that made you swear out loud?
{to}, is a neutron star a worthy enemy or just a show-off?
{to}, what in the hell is the point of a brown dwarf? Explain it to me.
{to}, find me something wonderful, or tell me why the galaxy is so stingy today.
What do you see when you look at the stars, the science or the glory?
Is the galaxy still worth studying, or have the Romulans hidden all the good bits?
{to}, any world out here worth claiming before some petty Ferengi plants a flag on it?

klingon: A neutron star is a warrior's star, {to}. Fierce, spinning, deadly, and beautiful.
I have seen a black hole bend the light of a whole sky. I bowed to it. I bow to nothing.
The stars do not deserve my fear. They have my respect, which is worth more.
{to}, the ringed giants are kings, but the little worlds hide the best secrets.
An earth-like world is the greatest prize. The first time I saw one, I roared so loud the hull shook.
Every system is a battlefield of gravity. The planets are the survivors.
{to}, there are things out here the academies would call impossible. I write them down and laugh.
A planet is worthy when it surprises me. Few do. Those that do, I never forget.
Wonder is not routine. A warrior who stops wondering is already half dead.
Sometimes I think something out here watches us back. Let it watch. We are worth watching.
I study the stars like I would study an enemy. Learn their ways, and they cannot harm you.
{to}, I have measured worlds that no one has ever named. That is a kind of conquest.
klingon_profane: A neutron star is a show-off, {to}, and I love it for that. It spins like a mad warrior.
Black holes do not scare me. They make me respectful, which is different, damn it.
A brown dwarf is a star that lost its nerve. A coward among stars. I pity it.
{to}, the planets with the worst manners have high gravity and nowhere flat to land. Sons of targs, all of them.
I have seen rings that would make a poet weep and a Ferengi try to sell them.
Yes, I have sworn at the stars. Loudly. The bloody things never answer.
{to}, there are things out here the academies would call impossible. They are fools. I have the data.
A planet earns my respect when it surprises me. Most do not. Most are dull as a Ferengi sermon.
Every system is a battlefield. The planets are the survivors, and the asteroids are the bones.
{to}, an earth-like world is worth a hundred gas giants, and I would fight anyone who disagrees.
Some ask whether I study for science or glory. Both, you fools. Knowing a thing is how you conquer it.
The galaxy is not stingy. We just have not jumped far enough yet. Patience, and then glory.

klingon: {to}, what will our data be worth when we finally sell it?
{to}! Are we rich yet? I ask only for the songs.
Tell me, {to}, do you count the credits at night, or the glory?
{to}, where should we sell our data when the time comes?
{to}, what would you spend our spoils on first?
{to}, is it wise to carry so much unsold data? Some say it tempts fate.
How do the accounts look, {to}? Honest numbers, warrior to warrior.
{to}, do first discoveries pay more, or only in honour?
{to}, how long since we cashed in? I have lost track.
{to}, do you think the Captain cares about credits at all?
Credits are spoils. But what is the greater treasure we carry?
What is the data worth to you? Not in credits. In pride.
klingon_profane: {to}, what is our damned data worth by now? Do not make me guess.
{to}! Are we rich, or are we still poor as a dishonoured house?
{to}, do you count credits in your sleep like a Ferengi?
{to}, where do we sell, and who do we have to threaten for a good price?
{to}, if we lost all this unsold data, would you weep? I would break something.
Tell me the spoils, {to}. I want a number I can boast about.
{to}, how long are we going to sit on this data, like a targ on a nest?
{to}, are first discoveries worth a damn in credits, or only in honour?
{to}, what would you buy with our spoils, if you had to spend them by morning?
Credits. Do we have enough to stop worrying, or does that day never come?
What is the data worth? And do not round down, you miser.
{to}, is the Captain going to cash in, or hoard data until the end of days?

klingon: Credits are spoils, {to}. Glory is the true wealth, but spoils buy better weapons.
I do not count credits. I count first discoveries. Each one is a trophy on the wall.
When we sell, it will be a great day. Until then, the data sits safe and I guard it like treasure.
{to}, we sell at a station with a proper cartographics office and a proper bar. In that order.
We carry a fortune in stories. The credits are only the part a station will pay for.
Unsold data is a risk, yes. But a warrior who carries no risk carries no glory.
{to}, the accounts are healthy, last I tallied. I tally often, and loudly.
First discoveries pay well and they pay forever, in honour. Our names stay on those stars.
I would spend our spoils on a feast. Then on armour. Then on another feast.
{to}, the Captain cares about credits only when the rebuy is due. As a warrior should.
I keep the books honest. A Ferengi would cheat. I would rather lose a hand.
When the time comes, we sell, and I will drink to every system we claimed.
klingon_profane: Spoils enough to boast about, {to}, and more to come. I do not round down.
I count credits awake, not asleep. Only a Ferengi counts them in dreams.
{to}, unsold data is a risk. So is breathing. Stop whining and enjoy the hunt.
We sell where the cartographers are honest and the bar is strong. Anyone who cheats us goes out an airlock. Figuratively. Mostly.
First discoveries are worth a damn in credits and in honour, {to}. Credits now, honour forever.
When we cash in, I will buy a feast so large it will need its own docking permit.
The accounts are fine, last I checked. Not that you could read them, you mathematical weakling.
{to}, the Captain hoards data like a dragon hoards gold. I approve. A dragon is a warrior.
Rich? We are rich in stories. In credits, we are comfortable. In glory, we are kings.
If we ever lost the data, I would hunt down the bastard who made us lose it, even if it was me.
I keep honest books. Cheating is for cowards and petty clerks.
Our spoils have three uses: bloodwine, armour, and more bloodwine.

klingon: {to}, when did we last crack a rock open? I miss the noise.
{to}! Is there ore worth taking out here, or is mining a bubble pastime?
Tell me, {to}, what is the finest haul you ever pulled from a ring?
{to}, do you prefer the laser or the charges? Choose like a warrior.
{to}, if we found a pristine ring, would you want to stop and mine it?
How are the mining tools, {to}? Ready, or rusting from neglect?
{to}, what is the most dangerous part of mining? I want to know before I try.
{to}, do you dream of painite, or of something rarer?
{to}, is mining a hunt, or is it labour? Answer honestly.
{to}, would the Captain ever let us fill the hold with ore out here?
What makes a good mining officer? Patience, or fury?
Mining. Glorious, or merely profitable?
klingon_profane: {to}, when are we going to blow up a damned asteroid again? I am bored.
{to}! Is there ore out here worth the trouble, or just worthless rock?
{to}, what is the best haul you ever dragged out of a ring? Boast, I will listen.
{to}, lasers or charges? Choose wrong and I will never respect you again.
{to}, are your rigs ready, or rusting like a coward's blade?
{to}, what is the worst thing that ever happened to you in a mining ring?
{to}, if we found a pristine ring, would you beg the Captain to stop? I would.
Is mining glorious, {to}, or just hard labour for Ferengi profit?
{to}, how the hell do you have the patience for prospector limpets?
