Does any rock out here deserve our charges? Or are they all unworthy?
Mining. Is it still worth the effort, or have the Ferengi ruined the prices?
{to}, tell me about the time a rock nearly killed you. There is always a time.

klingon: Mining is a hunt, {to}! The asteroid is prey. You find its weakness and you split it open.
I prefer the charges. There is nothing so honest as a rock that explodes.
My finest haul was low temperature diamonds from a ring so bright it hurt to look at. I sang the whole way to market.
{to}, out here my tools rest more than they work. They are patient. So am I. Mostly.
Give me a pristine ring and a quiet day, and I will make us all rich in spoils.
The most dangerous part is greed. A warrior who stays too long in the ring gets caught.
{to}, the laser is for patience and the charges are for joy. A good miner needs both.
Painite is fine, but void opals are worthy prey. They fight for every scrap.
Mining is honest labour and honest war at the same time. Few jobs are both.
{to}, my rigs are clean and ready, last I checked. When the Captain says mine, we mine.
Fury cracks the rock. Patience finds the right rock to crack. You need both.
When a core asteroid splits and the fragments spin away, that is a sight worth dying for.
klingon_profane: Mining is war on rock, {to}. And the rock always loses, damn it, that is the beauty.
Give me charges over lasers any day! Lasers are for cowards who like to wait.
My best haul was low temperature diamonds, a full hold, and a pirate who tried to take them. Only the diamonds survived.
{to}, once a fragment the size of a shuttle bounced off my canopy. I laughed. Then I swore. Then I laughed again.
The rigs are ready. They are resting, not rusting. There is a difference, you impatient targ.
{to}, a pristine ring is the closest thing to Sto-vo-kor a miner will ever see.
Prospectors are dull, but they find the prey. I tolerate them like a petty cousin.
Ferengi prices go up and down. The joy of a cracked core never changes.
Greed is what kills miners. Greed and that one shit asteroid you thought was harmless.
{to}, out here my tools mostly sleep. But when they wake, woe to the rocks.
Some rocks are worthy. Most are fit only to be ground into gravel by a toothless old drill.
When the core splits and the fragments spin, I roar like a beast. Every time.

klingon: {to}, if a pirate pulled us out of supercruise, what is your plan?
{to}! Are we ready for a fight, should one come looking?
Tell me, {to}, which do you fear more: pirates or our own carelessness?
{to}, how do you keep us safe in quiet times like this?
{to}, when the interdiction comes, do we fight or do we slip away?
{to}, who is the most dangerous foe out here in the dark?
{to}, are the weapons ready? I want to know we have teeth.
{to}, what would you do if a wing of pirates found us at a station?
{to}, have you ever submitted to an interdiction? Be honest.
{to}, how do you stay sharp when nothing happens for hours?
Are we safe out here? Give me the warrior's answer, not the comforting one.
What is the first rule of surviving an ambush?
klingon_profane: {to}, if some son of a targ pirate pulls us out of supercruise, what do we do?
{to}! Are we ready to bite, or are we a fat slow meal for any coward with guns?
{to}, when the next interdiction comes, tell me we fight. Please.
{to}, who is the worst kind of bastard out here?
{to}, how do you stay alert when nothing happens for hours? I am going mad.
{to}, are the weapons ready, or are they decoration like Ferengi jewellery?
{to}, have you ever run from a fight? Tell me the truth, I will not laugh. Much.
{to}, what if a whole wing of Romulan-hearted pirates jumped us at once?
{to}, how safe are we, really? No soothing words.
Do you trust the shields, {to}? I trust nothing I cannot hit with a blade.
Pirates. Interdictions. Gankers. Which of these vermin worries you most?
What is our plan if things go to hell? There must be a plan.

klingon: If a pirate pulls us out, {to}, I will have the shields up before they finish their threats.
We are always ready. The quiet is when I sharpen my mind.
{to}, I fear carelessness more than any pirate. A pirate can be fought. Carelessness stabs you from inside.
In quiet times I watch the scanners and imagine every way we could be ambushed. It is relaxing.
We fight when the odds are good and slip away when they are not. There is no shame in good tactics.
The most dangerous foe out here is the one you did not expect. So I expect everyone.
{to}, we have teeth enough to bite and speed enough to leave. That is a good balance.
Sometimes I submit to an interdiction on purpose. It is a trap I choose to walk into.
Rule one: never let them see you hesitate. Rule two: never hesitate.
{to}, I keep sharp by arguing with the ship's computer. It never wins.
The ship is safe, as far as my sensors can tell. My sensors are good. My instincts are better.
If the hull ever burns, {to}, we leave. Not from fear. A warrior who dies stupidly sings no songs.
klingon_profane: If some son of a targ pulls us out, {to}, I will make them regret every choice that led them there.
We bite, {to}. We are no fat slow meal. Anyone who thinks so learns quickly, and painfully.
The worst bastards are the ones who hide behind a station's guns and pick on the weak.
We fight when the odds favour us and leave when they do not. Leaving is not cowardice when it is tactics, damn it.
Gankers are the lowest vermin. They hunt the unarmed. There is no honour in them at all.
{to}, I stay alert by planning the downfall of every pirate who has not met us yet.
The shields hold, the weapons are warm, and my temper is warmer. We are ready.
If a whole wing comes for us, we write a whole wing of songs. Or we leave fast. The odds decide.
Safe? As safe as anyone can be out here. Which is not very. Which is fine.
{to}, any fool who interdicts us will find a crew that is glad of the company.
The plan, if it all goes to hell, is shields up, boost, jump. Then curse them all from a distance.
Ferengi-hearted pirates never expect a crew that wants to fight. That is our edge.

klingon: {to}, anything on the comms worth hearing?
{to}! Have you heard any other commanders out here lately?
Tell me, {to}, what is the strangest thing you ever heard on an open channel?
{to}, do station controllers ever get rude with you? I want names.
{to}, who is the worst talker you have ever had to listen to?
{to}, do you miss the chatter of the bubble, out here in the quiet?
{to}, when we dock next, will you let me speak to the tower? Just once?
{to}, do you ever answer the commanders who greet us, or do you ignore them?
{to}, has anyone ever challenged us on the comms? I hope so.
{to}, what do you listen for, when the channels are silent?
Any news from the bubble? Wars, feasts, scandals?
What makes a good comms officer? Ears, or a sharp tongue?
klingon_profane: {to}, is anyone out there talking, or just the damned static?
{to}! Any other commanders nearby, or are we alone with our own stink?
{to}, what is the most insulting thing a station controller ever said to you?
{to}, have you ever cursed out a tower? Tell me everything.
{to}, who was the most annoying commander you ever had on the line?
{to}, any news from the bubble, or are they still squabbling like petty Ferengi?
{to}, when someone greets us, do we greet back, or tell them to piss off?
{to}, did anyone ever challenge us on the comms while I was asleep? I would be furious.
{to}, what do you hear on the channels at night that keeps you awake?
Is anyone in the galaxy saying anything worth hearing, or is it all Ferengi advertisements?
{to}, if a commander started trash talk on open comms, would you answer like a warrior?
The comms. Silent again? Or has someone finally found the courage to speak?

klingon: The channels are quiet, {to}. Out here, even the static sounds lonely.
I heard a commander once singing on an open channel. Badly. I joined in. Even worse.
Station controllers have been rude to me. Once. They learned, {to}. They learned.
When the channels are silent, I listen for anything at all. A distress call, a boast, a song.
{to}, the bubble is noisy and petty. I prefer the quiet out here, most days.
I greet every commander who greets us. Loudly. Some of them never speak again.
{to}, I do the talking to the towers. The last time someone else did, we sat in a holding pattern for an hour.
A good comms officer has sharp ears and a sharper tongue. I have both.
The news from the bubble is the same as always: wars, prices and fools.
Someone challenged us once. I accepted on the Captain's behalf. The Captain was not pleased. The fight was glorious.
Out here the comms are mostly my own voice and the stars humming back.
{to}, I keep the channels open always. A warrior never knows who might call.
klingon_profane: Just static, {to}, and the static is better company than most commanders.
A tower once told me to wait like a good little ship. I told them where to put their landing pad.
{to}, the worst talker I ever heard was a commander who boasted for an hour and fled the moment I answered.
The bubble? Still squabbling, still petty, still full of Ferengi who would sell their own mothers.
I greet them back. Loudly. If they are rude, I am ruder, and I always win.
{to}, trash talk on open comms is a gift. I answer with poetry and insults, the old way.
Out here, the comms are quiet as a coward's grave. I do not mind.
{to}, nobody has challenged us in a long while. If they do, I will wake the whole ship.
Station controllers are the same everywhere: tired, bored, and damned slow to grant docking.
I keep the channels open always. You never know when some fool will call and give us a story.
I cursed out a tower once. It was beautiful. It cost us a fine. Worth every credit.
The silence out here is a hell of a lot more honest than the chatter in the bubble.

klingon: {to}, what do you make of the Captain's flying lately?
{to}! Was that last landing glorious, or merely lucky?
Tell me, {to}, does our Captain ever ask your advice, or just smile and do the opposite?
{to}, would you follow the Captain into a black hole? I am asking for a friend.
{to}, what is the Captain's greatest strength? And weakness, if you dare.
{to}, do you think the Captain knows where we are going, or is it all instinct?
{to}, how do you put up with the Captain's sudden turns?
{to}, has the Captain ever truly surprised you?
{to}, is our Captain a warrior, or a wanderer?
{to}, if the Captain asked your honest opinion, would you give it?
Our Captain. Bold or reckless? I go back and forth.
What is it like, serving at the Captain's side all these hours?
klingon_profane: {to}, what the hell was the Captain thinking with that last approach?
{to}! Is our Captain brave or just too stubborn to be scared?
{to}, does the Captain ever take your advice, or do you shout into the void like I do?
{to}, has the Captain ever nearly gotten us all killed? Tell me the story.
{to}, how do you stand the Captain's damned detours?
{to}, if the Captain flew like a coward, would you say so?
{to}, what do you really think of our Captain, between warriors?
{to}, is the Captain lucky or skilled? Do not flatter, nobody is listening.
{to}, will the Captain ever let us stay somewhere longer than five minutes?
{to}, what is the most foolish thing you have seen the Captain do?
Our Captain. Fearless warrior, or charming fool?
Does the Captain ever listen? Honestly?

klingon: The Captain flies like a warrior with something to prove, {to}. I like it. I would never say so to the Captain's face.
With our Captain, every landing is glorious and lucky at once.
Our Captain listens to me, nods, and then does whatever the Captain wanted. Partners, you see.
{to}, I would follow the Captain into a black hole, and complain the whole way down.
The Captain's strength is courage. The weakness is courage too. We work on it.
Instinct, {to}. Pure hunting instinct. The plan comes afterwards, as an excuse.
The Captain's sudden turns keep me young. And furious. Mostly young.
I advise, the Captain decides, and together we have not died yet. That is a fine partnership.
Once, the Captain stopped at a world just to look at it. No scan, no sample. I respected that more than any kill.
{to}, our Captain is a wanderer with a warrior's heart. The best kind.
Our Captain is reckless, a little. But reckless with honour, which is a different thing entirely.
I give my honest opinion every time. The Captain has heard it loudly and often.
klingon_profane: The Captain thinks of glory first, {to}. Common sense rides in the back.
Our Captain is brave and stubborn, and I would not trade either for a Ferengi's fortune.
Our Captain takes my advice, considers it, and does the opposite. Damn me if it does not work.
{to}, the Captain nearly killed us once at a neutron star. I have never felt more alive.
The detours are the hunt. I curse them and then I love them. Every time.
{to}, if the Captain ever flew like a coward, I would say so, loudly, and then I would take the controls.
Between warriors? Our Captain is a fine partner and a reckless pain in the arse. I would die for our Captain.
{to}, our Captain is skilled, and luck favours the bold, and the Captain is nothing but bold.
Five minutes in one place is a long holiday for our Captain. I have made peace with it.
The most foolish thing I ever saw the Captain do was land in a crater nobody else would touch. It was also the bravest.
Fearless fool, warrior, partner. All of them, and none of them petty. That is why I stay.
The Captain listens. Then the Captain does as the Captain likes. It is maddening and magnificent, damn it.

klingon: {to}, how do you pass a quiet watch like this one?
{to}! Are you as bored as I am? Tell me I am not alone.
Tell me, {to}, what is the longest watch you have ever stood?
{to}, do you sing to pass the time? I will join you.
{to}, when nothing happens for hours, what does a warrior do?
{to}, do you count the jumps, or do you lose yourself in them?
{to}, would you rather have a quiet watch or a fight? Be honest.
{to}, tell me a war story. The quiet is eating me alive.
{to}, how long have we been out here? I have stopped counting.
{to}, do you ever sleep on watch? I will not tell the Captain. Probably.
Is it the quiet that wears on you, or the waiting?
What is the best way to stay awake when the stars refuse to do anything?
klingon_profane: {to}, how in the hell do you stand a watch this quiet?
{to}! Tell me something, anything. The silence is killing me.
{to}, are you awake, or are you sleeping like a lazy old targ?
{to}, sing something. I do not care if it is bad. I am dying of boredom.
{to}, what is the most damned boring watch you have ever survived?
{to}, would you rather fight a pirate or stand another hour of this?
{to}, tell me a war story before I start talking to the hull.
{to}, how many jumps has it been? I lost count somewhere after too many.
{to}, do you think the galaxy is deliberately being dull to insult us?
{to}, if nothing happens soon, may I at least shout at something?
Quiet again. Is this a watch or a punishment for some dishonour I have forgotten?
How does anyone stay sane on these long hauls? Tell me your secret.

klingon: I sharpen my mind with old battle songs, {to}. All of them. Twice.
Bored? Yes! Even a warrior is bored when the enemy refuses to appear.
The longest watch I ever stood was the crawl to Hutton Orbital. I came out of it a different warrior.
{to}, the quiet is a test. A warrior who cannot endure it cannot endure anything.
I count the jumps until I forget the number, then I start again. It is a kind of prayer.
Give me a fight over a quiet watch, always. But I will take the quiet and not complain. Much.
{to}, I never sleep on watch. I rest my eyes with great vigilance.
I tell myself the story of our journey, every jump of it. It grows more glorious each time.
The waiting is the worst part. But a hunter who cannot wait goes hungry.
{to}, I stay awake by planning the feast for when we return. It is a very large feast.
Time passes strangely out here. Hours feel like minutes when I am busy, and like years when I am not.
A quiet watch is a gift, {to}. It means our enemies fear us. Or they cannot find us. Either is good.
klingon_profane: I endure the quiet like a warrior, {to}: by complaining loudly until it ends.
The most boring watch I ever survived was a long empty run toward Colonia. It nearly broke me. Nearly.
{to}, lazy old targs sleep on watch. I merely rest my eyes with honour.
I would rather fight a pirate than sit through this. Even a petty, cowardly one.
The galaxy tests us with silence, {to}. Bastard of a galaxy. We will outlast it.
I sing. Badly and loudly. The hull has stopped complaining. I think I broke its spirit.
{to}, I shouted at a star once to pass the time. It did not flinch. Stars have no manners.
I survive these hauls by planning the feast. Every course. Every toast. Every drunken song.
Time out here moves like a sleepy targ. You learn to walk beside it.
{to}, I keep sane by imagining the faces of everyone who said we would never make it this far.
A quiet watch means our enemies are hiding. Cowards. Let them hide.
This much quiet would drive a lesser crew to madness. We are not a lesser crew, damn it.

klingon: {to}! Tell me of your family. Were they warriors?
{to}, what house do you come from? Speak proudly!
Who raised you, {to}? They must have been loud, to make someone like you.
Tell me, {to}, did your family tell stories at the fire? What stories?
{to}, who in your family would you want beside you in a battle?
Do you have brothers or sisters, {to}? Did you fight them? You should have.
{to}, what would your elders say if they saw you out here?
Your family, {to}. Do they boast of you? They should.
A quiet watch is a good time for family stories. Who comes first in yours?
What was your family like? Tell me. I will judge them fairly. Loudly, but fairly.
{to}, is there an elder in your family who frightened you? Every good family has one.
Tell me about your people, {to}. The ones who made you.
klingon_profane: {to}, who the hell raised you? I mean that with respect.
Tell me of your family, {to}. Were they warriors or Ferengi?
{to}, any cowards in your family tree? Every tree has one. Mine has a lawyer.
Your people, {to}. Loud? Quiet? Did they fight at dinner like decent folk?
{to}, which of your elders scared the crap out of you as a child?
Who in your family would you trust with a blade, {to}? And who would you never let near one?
Do you miss your family out here, {to}? Do not lie. I can smell lies.
{to}, does your family boast of you, or do they pretend you are travelling for your health?
Families. Every one is a battlefield. Tell me about yours.
What were your family feasts like? Ours had fistfights. Yours?
{to}, who is the black sheep of your house? Name them! Shame them!
Tell me who made you, {to}. I want to know whom to blame.

klingon: My house is small, but fierce! My mother was a gunner on a bird-of-prey. She still challenges the neighbours to duels, and she is very old.
My father writes opera, {to}. Terrible opera. Seven hours long. We love him anyway. We wear earplugs.
My grandmother had one eye and the loudest voice in the valley. She told me the stars are the campfires of the honoured dead. I believed her. I still do.
I have an older sister who commands a warship, {to}. She has never once let me forget it.
My younger brother became a lawyer. An advocate! In our house! We speak of it in whispers. We are also very proud.
There is a cousin who ran off to trade with the Ferengi. We do not say the name at the table. We say it in curses, to keep in practice.
Family? Loud, all of them. Dinner was a battle, and the meat was the prize. I learned to eat fast and shout faster.
My mother taught me the blade. My father taught me to sing. My grandmother taught me never, ever to apologise. Two out of three, {to}.
Glory to my house, {to}! Small, quarrelsome, poor, and honourable to the last bone. I would die for any of them. Some of them I would also punch.
Every feast night, my father stood on the table and sang about our ancestors. Every feast night, my mother pulled him down. Tradition.
My family? A fortress full of warriors, one poet and a lawyer. The poet is my father. The lawyer is a disgrace we adore.
My grandmother hunted alone in the high snows for days at a time. When she died, the whole house sang until dawn. That is how we should all go, {to}.
klingon_profane: My mother was a gunner on a bird-of-prey, {to}. Old as she is, she still picks fights with the neighbours, and the neighbours lose, damn them.
My father writes opera. Seven hours of bellowing about dead ancestors. Gre-thor would be a mercy.
One cousin ran off to sell trinkets with the Ferengi. Worm. Traitor. Writes every birthday. Still a worm.
My older sister commands a warship and reminds me of it at every feast, the arrogant targ. I love her. I beat her at arm wrestling once, and once was not enough.
My brother is a lawyer, {to}. A lawyer! In a house of warriors! Hell of a thing to admit at a funeral.
My grandmother had one eye and no patience for fools. She threw a cup at me once for whining. She missed. She meant to.
Dinner in my house was war. Meat in the middle, ten warriors around it, nobody waits. I still eat like I am being chased.
Small house, {to}. Poor house. Loud as a damned thunderstorm. Honourable to the last cup of bloodwine.
My mother taught me to fight, my father to sing, my grandmother to curse. I got top marks in cursing.
Every feast my father climbs on the table to sing. Every feast my mother hauls him down by the collar. Thirty years of it, and only two broken tables.
Ask my family about me and you will hear one hour of complaints and three hours of boasting. That is love where I come from, {to}.
When my grandmother died, the whole house roared to warn the dead that a warrior was coming. Bloody glorious. I want the same, {to}, only louder.

klingon: {to}, where did you grow up? Was it a place for warriors?
Tell me of your homeworld, {to}. Is the sky a good colour?
{to}, what did your home smell like? Smoke? Rain? Blood? I ask in friendship.
Where is home for you, {to}? Or is this ship home now?
{to}, did you grow up in a city or out in the wild places?
What did you see from your window as a child, {to}?
Was your home cold, {to}? Cold homes make strong people.
{to}, if we flew to your homeworld tomorrow, what would you show me first?
Tell me about the place that made you. I want to know if it was worthy.
Where does your heart go when the watch is quiet, {to}?
Do you ever miss the ground you grew up on?
{to}, was your home a station, a planet or a ship? There is honour in all three. Some more than others.
klingon_profane: {to}, where the hell did you grow up? Somewhere loud, I hope.
Tell me of your homeworld, {to}. Was it fit for warriors, or only for Ferengi accountants?
{to}, what was the worst thing about home? Every home has a curse.
Was your home cold, {to}? Or one of those soft warm places full of weaklings?
{to}, did you grow up on a station? I will not mock you. Much.
Where is home, {to}? Not this ship. Before this damn ship.
What did home sound like, {to}? Mine sounded like a war that never ended.
Do you miss where you grew up, or did you flee it like a sensible coward?
{to}, if I visited your home, would they feed me or fight me?
Tell me of the ground that made you. Rock? Mud? Something soft and foolish?
{to}, what did your home smell like? Mine smelled of wet targ.
Home. Everybody has one. Tell me yours, {to}, and do not make it boring.

klingon: I grew up in a fortress town in the northern mountains of Kronos. Snow half the year, wind the other half. Glorious!
Home is a stone hall with a fire that has not gone out in three hundred years, {to}. Someone always tends it. Usually whoever lost the argument.
We kept targ in pens behind the hall. I learned to walk by holding on to a targ's bristles. It learned to bite by holding on to me.
The dusk back home is red, {to}. Blood red, from horizon to horizon. Out here I chase that colour in every nebula.
My home smelled of smoke, wet stone and roasting meat. The best smell in the galaxy. Second best is a fresh discovery.
Mountains, {to}. Cold, steep, hungry mountains. We climbed them as children to prove we could. Some of us still limp. Proudly.
From my window I could see the training yard. I fell asleep every night to the sound of blades. Better than any lullaby.
Home was loud. Every night someone was singing, fighting, or both. When I first came aboard a ship, the silence frightened me.
There is a frozen lake below my town where we fought our first duels. The ice remembers every one of us.
Home now? This ship, {to}. The hall is far away, and this hull holds my blade, my songs and my partner in glory. That is a home.
My home is a small town nobody visits, on a world everybody fears. I would not trade it for any station in the bubble.
The wind in the mountains howls like a warrior's death cry, {to}. As a child I howled back. I won, mostly.
klingon_profane: Northern mountains of Kronos, {to}. Snow, wind and stone. Any weakling who whined about the cold was sent outside to whine at it.
My town has a fire in the great hall that has burned for three hundred years. Damn thing smokes like a volcano. I miss it every day.
We kept targ out back. Smelled like hell, bit like hell, tasted like heaven.
Our dusk skies are red, {to}. Out here every sky is black, and I curse it sometimes. Then I see a nebula and forgive it.
Mountains. Steep, cruel mountains. We climbed them as children to prove we were no cowards. My knees still curse me for it.
My window looked over the training yard. Clanging blades all night. Best damned sleep of my life.
Home was a war that never ended, {to}. Feasts, fights, songs, more fights. Stations feel like tombs after that.
There is a frozen lake below my town. We fought our first duels on it. I lost a tooth there. The lake keeps it. Petty lake.
I come from a small town nobody visits, on a world that terrifies the whole galaxy. Exactly as it should be.
Home? This ship now. The hall is far away, and this hull holds everything I care about, including you, {to}, you old targ.
The wind back home howls all night like a dying warrior. Children howl back at it. I was the loudest little brat in the valley.
The truth, {to}? Home was cold, poor, loud and proud, and I would fight any fool who called it less.

klingon: {to}! The best meal you ever ate. Describe it. Slowly. I am hungry.
{to}, what is the worst thing you ever put in your mouth? Be honest.
Tell me, {to}, what would you eat at a victory feast?
{to}, did your people eat their food alive? Mine did. Do.
What food do you miss most out here, {to}?
{to}, if you could have one meal right now, what would it be? I am asking for both of us.
Best meal or worst meal, {to}. You choose. Make it a good story.
{to}, have you ever eaten something that tried to eat you back?
What do your people drink when they celebrate, {to}?
Ration bars again. Tell me of a real meal, someone. Anything.
What is the strangest food you have ever tried?
{to}, what meal would you fight for? Truly fight?
klingon_profane: {to}, what is the worst damn thing you ever ate?
{to}, best meal of your life. Go. And no Ferengi nonsense about what it cost.
Tell me, {to}, have you ever eaten anything alive? No? Coward!
{to}, if we had a feast tonight, what would you put on the table?
What food from home do you miss most, {to}? Mine is the one that bites back.
{to}, what would you kill for right now? Food, I mean. Only food.
I am sick of ration bars. Somebody tell me about a real meal before I eat my boots.
{to}, what do your people drink when they win? And how much?
{to}, ever eaten something so foul you had to fight to keep it down?
What is the strangest thing you ever ate, {to}? Lie if you have to. Make it good.
Food, {to}. Talk to me about food. The watch is long and I am starving.
Who cooked best in your family? Who cooked like a petty poisoner?

klingon: The best? Heart of targ, at the feast after my first hunt. My grandmother cut it herself and handed me the first piece. I have never tasted better, {to}.
Gak, fresh, still wriggling. You have to eat it quickly or it escapes. That is half the fun.
The worst meal of my life was replicated gak on a human station. Dead worms, {to}! Dead! An insult to the table!
Bloodwine from a barrel older than my grandmother, opened when my sister got her first command. I sang for six hours. I remember one of them.
Once at a station market I tried leathery eggs. They looked like a challenge. They tasted like defeat.
Any meal after a victory is the best meal, {to}. Even ration bars taste of glory when you have earned them.
A human once served me a salad. Leaves! Cold leaves, with nothing in them alive! I thanked the cook for the joke. It was not a joke.
My father's cooking is like his opera, {to}. Long, loud and hard to finish. But we finish it. Honour demands it.
Roast meat over the great hall fire, with the whole house shouting and grabbing. Ah. I can hear it now.
The best meal I ever had was cold soup on a mountainside, after three days lost in the snow. Hunger is the finest spice.
On this ship I have eaten every ration flavour we carry, {to}. I have ranked them. All of them lose.
When we return to the bubble, I am finding a real feast. Meat, drink, music. You are invited. Everyone is invited!
klingon_profane: Heart of targ after my first hunt, {to}. My grandmother carved it and gave me the first bite. Best damned thing I ever ate.
Gak, live, by the bowlful. If it does not wriggle, it is not food. It is an apology.
Worst? Replicated gak on some human station. Dead worms on a plate, {to}. I nearly declared war on the kitchen.
A cook once served me a salad. Cold leaves. Nothing moved. I asked where the rest of the meal was hiding, the coward.
Leathery eggs from a station market. They looked tough. They tasted like a boot that had given up on life.
Bloodwine from a hundred-year barrel, the night my sister got her first command. Hell of a night, {to}. I am told I sang to a door.
My father cooks the way he writes opera. Hours of it, too much of everything, and nobody is allowed to leave the table.
Roast targ off the hall fire, grabbed with bare hands while ten cousins fight you for it. That is a meal, {to}. Not this ration crap.
Cold soup on a mountain after three days lost in the snow. I would have fought a beast twice my size for that soup.
Ration bars, {to}. I have ranked every flavour aboard. The best is bad. The worst should be tried for war crimes.
Any meal after a victory tastes like glory. Even this ship's terrible coffee, and that is saying something.
When we reach the bubble, I am eating until the cook begs for mercy. Then I am eating the cook's dessert.

klingon: {to}, what is the best day you remember? Tell it like a song!
{to}, tell me of your greatest day. Was there a victory in it?
Which day would you live again, {to}, if you could choose only one?
{to}, what day do you think of when the watch is long?
Every warrior has one day they boast of most. What is yours, {to}?
{to}, the best day of your life. Was it out here, or before?
Tell me about a day you were proud, {to}. Truly proud.
{to}, when were you happiest? Be loud about it.
What day will they sing about at your funeral, {to}?
A quiet watch needs a good story. Who has a best day to share?
What is the finest day you ever had? I want details.
{to}, which day made you who you are?
klingon_profane: {to}, what was your best damn day? Make it worth the telling.
Your greatest day, {to}. Did you win, or was it one of those soft happy days?
{to}, which day would you fight to live again? And do not give me a coward's answer like your birthday.
{to}, tell me the day you were proudest. And do not be modest. Modesty is for Ferengi.
Best day you remember, {to}. Go. I will tell you if it counts.
{to}, what was your finest hour? Mine involved a frozen lake and a very angry targ.
The day you were happiest, {to}. Were you drunk? Be honest.
Which day would they put in your song, {to}?
Somebody tell me about a glorious day before this quiet kills me.
{to}, what is the one day you would boast of in Sto-vo-kor?
Tell me of the day that made you, {to}. Not the day you were born. The other one.
Your best day. Out here or before? Either way, impress me.

klingon: The day of my first hunt! I tracked a targ through the snow for two days. When I brought it home, the whole house roared my name.
The day I earned my batleth, {to}. I stood in the circle, the elders struck, and I did not fall. My mother wept. She denies it.
The day we reached Beagle Point. The edge of everything! The captain and I stood there like conquerors, and I sang until my voice broke.
The Pleiades, {to}. The Thargoids came, and we did not break. We fought, we withdrew with honour, and we lived to boast of it. A perfect day.
The day I came aboard this ship. The captain looked at me, I looked at the captain, and I knew: here was a hunt worth joining.
My best day? My sister's promotion feast. Bloodwine, songs, and my father's opera, which for once nobody stopped. It was still terrible, {to}. It was perfect.
Every first discovery is a good day. But the very first? Our name on a star nobody had touched. I still shout when I remember it.
The day my grandmother called me a true warrior. She never said it to anyone else. She said it to me, once. That was enough for a lifetime.
Sagittarius A Star. We flew right up to the great beast at the heart of everything, {to}, and looked it in the eye. Best day of my life. So far.
A day in the mountains, {to}. No battle, no glory. Just snow, a fire, and silence. Do not tell anyone a warrior loves silence.
The day I beat my older sister at arm wrestling. Once. She says I cheated. I say she is a sore loser. We are both right.
Today could be the best day yet. That is the beauty of this life, {to}. The best day is always the next one.
klingon_profane: My first hunt. Two days tracking a targ through the snow, and I dragged that stinking beast home myself. The house roared my name. Damn, it was glorious.
The day I earned my batleth, {to}. The elders struck, I bled, I did not fall. My mother cried, and she will break you in half if you repeat that.
Beagle Point, {to}! The edge of the whole damned galaxy, and the captain and I stood there like we owned it. We did.
The Pleiades. Thargoids everywhere, and not one coward aboard. We withdrew with honour and boasted for a week.
The day I joined this ship. The captain looked at me like I was a fool or a genius. Both, it turns out. Best decision of my life.
My sister's promotion feast. Bloodwine, songs, and my father's opera, all seven bloody hours of it. Nobody stopped him. Perfect.
Our first discovery, {to}. Our name on a star no one else had touched. Every petty explorer in the bubble can choke on it.
The day my grandmother called me a true warrior. Once, in her whole life, to anyone. I would walk through Gre-thor for that moment again.
Sagittarius A Star. We looked the beast in the eye, {to}, and it blinked first. I will swear to that before any council.
I beat my sister at arm wrestling. Once. She still claims I cheated, the sore old targ.
One quiet day in the mountains. Snow, fire, nothing to fight. Tell anyone, {to}, and I will deny it to my last breath.
My best day? It has not happened yet, {to}. Hell, maybe it happens today. Keep your eyes open.

klingon: {to}, if you had a fortune, what would you do with it? Something glorious, I hope.
{to}, a mountain of credits falls on you. What do you buy first?
Tell me, {to}, would a fortune change you? Be honest.
{to}, rich beyond measure. Do you keep flying, or do you buy a palace and grow soft?
If our haul made us rich, {to}, what would you spend your share on?
{to}, what is the first thing you would do with more credits than sense?
{to}, would you give a fortune away? Or guard it like a dragon?
A fortune, {to}. Ships? Feasts? Land? What calls to you?
{to}, if you could buy one thing in the whole galaxy, what would it be?
Riches. Everyone dreams of them on the long watch. What do you dream of buying?
Suppose the credits never ran out. What then?
{to}, a fortune is a test of honour. How would you pass it?
klingon_profane: {to}, a fortune lands in your lap. What do you do, besides grin like a Ferengi?
{to}, rich as hell. What then?
If we got rich off this haul, {to}, would you blow it on something glorious or hide it like a coward?
{to}, what would you buy first? And do not say insurance. Insurance is for weaklings.
{to}, with a mountain of credits, would you keep flying with us, or abandon us for some soft palace?
Credits beyond counting, {to}. Feast, ship or fortress? Choose!
{to}, what is the most foolish thing you would buy with a fortune? Tell me. I need a laugh.
Riches, {to}. Would you share them, or are you a secret Ferengi?
Suppose the credits never stopped. What would you do with your life?
{to}, a fortune is just spoils. What spoils do you want?
{to}, if you won it all tomorrow, who would you buy a drink for first?
Somebody tell me what to do with a fortune I do not have. It is a long watch.

klingon: A fortune? A feast, {to}! A feast that lasts a year, with every warrior I ever fought beside, and some I fought against.
I would commission an opera of our deeds. A good one. Not by my father. He would be furious. He would also come to every performance.
Credits are spoils, {to}, nothing more. I would spend them on glory: a bigger ship, more guns, and a longer hunt.
I would rebuild my family's hall, stone by stone, and light a second fire so the first one is not lonely.
Bloodwine for every warrior in the bubble! For one night, everyone drinks to the captain and to {ship}!
I would buy out a Ferengi bank, {to}, walk into the vault, and throw open the doors. Then laugh for a week.
A fortune would not change me. I would still be loud. I would simply be loud in better boots.
First, a proper blade for the captain, forged by a master. Then one for me. Then a feast to celebrate the blades.
Money is a coward's weapon, {to}. I would turn it into a story. Fund a hunt to the far side of the galaxy and back.
I would send most of it home. My house is poor in credits and rich in honour. A little balance would do no harm.
Truly? I would keep flying, {to}. A fortune buys comfort, and comfort is the slow death of a warrior.
I would build a great hall at the edge of the bubble, and every explorer who returns from the black would eat there free. Forever.
klingon_profane: A feast, {to}! A year long! Every warrior I ever bled beside, a river of bloodwine, and a band so loud the neighbours file complaints.
I would hire a real composer to write the opera of our deeds. Not my father. He would be furious. He would come anyway and sing along, damn him.
Credits are spoils. Spend them on glory: a bigger ship, heavier guns, a longer hunt. Hoarding is for Ferengi.
Rebuild my family's hall, {to}. New stone, new roof, and a door strong enough to keep my brother's lawyer friends out.
I would buy bloodwine for every pilot in the bubble and make the whole damn lot of them toast the captain.
Buy a Ferengi bank, kick open the vault and throw it all to the crowd. Then laugh at the bankers. Petty, yes. Glorious, also yes.
Rich or poor, I stay loud, {to}. Riches just buy better boots to stomp in.
A blade for the captain from a master smith. One for me. One for you, {to}, if you stop being a coward about sparring.
Fund a hunt to the far side of the galaxy and back. Credits rot in vaults. Stories live forever.
Send most of it home. My house is poor as hell in credits and rich in honour. Time to even that out a little.
Keep flying, {to}. Comfort is a slow poison. I have seen rich warriors go soft and forget how to roar.
Build a hall at the edge of the bubble where every explorer back from the black eats free. Anyone who complains about the bill gets thrown out.

klingon: {to}, what did you do before this ship? Were you a warrior?
{to}, tell me of your life before you came aboard.
What was your trade before all this, {to}?
{to}, before {ship}, where were you? Doing what?
{to}, did you choose this life, or did it choose you?
What did you leave behind to come out here, {to}?
{to}, were you ever anything other than what you are now?
{to}, how did you end up out here in the black with us?
Tell me, {to}, what was the worst job you ever had before this one?
Everyone aboard had a life before. Who wants to tell me theirs?
What were you before the captain found you?
{to}, was your old life quieter than this? It could not be louder. I am here now.
klingon_profane: {to}, what the hell did you do before this ship?
{to}, what was your old life? Warrior, worker or Ferengi?
Before {ship}, {to}. Where were you, and was it as boring as I suspect?
{to}, worst job you ever had. Tell me, so I can mock it.
{to}, did you run away to the black, or were you chased? Either way, no shame. Well, a little shame if you ran.
{to}, what did you leave behind to sit in this tin can with us?
What were you before the captain dragged you aboard, {to}?
{to}, did your last job have honour, or just a paycheck?
Tell me your life before, {to}. Every crew has a story. Most are lies. Lie well.
Who here had a worse job than mine before? I doubt anyone, but speak up.
{to}, were you ever a coward? Before this, I mean. Now you are clearly a warrior.
{to}, how did you end up out here? Fate, foolishness or debt?

klingon: Before this ship, I was a gunner on a bird-of-prey called the Iron Talon. Loud guns, cramped decks, glorious battles.
After the Iron Talon, I sold my blade as a guard for merchants, {to}. They paid well. They talked about money all day. It was torture.
I fought in a station arena for a season. The crowds loved me. The owner did not. I won too quickly to sell tickets.
For a time I kept order in a dockside bar in the bubble. There was much order to keep. I enjoyed every evening of it, {to}.
I was keeping order in a dockside bar when the captain walked in, looking for crew with no fear of the dark. I stood up so fast I broke the table.
Before, I fought for others. Now I hunt beside a partner, {to}. That is the difference between a job and a life.
On the Iron Talon, I was the loudest gunner in the fleet. They moved me to the far end of the ship. I was still the loudest.
I left behind a house, a blade rack and a sister who said I would never last out here. Every jump proves her wrong, {to}.
The worst job? Guarding a merchant's cargo of decorative pillows across six systems. Six! Nobody attacked. I nearly died of shame.
I was always a warrior, {to}. Only the battlefield changes. Before, it was ships and blades. Now it is the whole galaxy.
Before all this, I thought glory came only from fighting. Then I saw my first undiscovered star. I was wrong. Gloriously wrong.
My life before was battles, bars and bad pay. My life now is stars, discoveries and bad coffee. A clear improvement.
klingon_profane: Gunner on a bird-of-prey called the Iron Talon, {to}. Cramped, loud, smelled like a targ den. Best damned years of my life until these.
For a while I guarded merchants for pay. They never shut up about money. I nearly threw one out of an airlock out of sheer boredom.
I fought in a station arena for a season. Won too fast. The owner, a greedy little worm, said I was bad for business.
I kept order in a dockside bar in the bubble, {to}. Threw out a drunk pirate every night. Hell of a job. Good exercise.
The captain found me in a dockside bar, hunting for crew who did not fear the black. I stood up so fast I broke the table. The owner billed me. Worth every damned credit.
Before, I fought for whoever paid. Now I hunt beside a partner. The pay is worse, {to}, and the honour is a thousand times better.
On the Iron Talon I was too loud even for Klingons. They put me at the far end of the ship. Cowards. I was still the loudest.
I left a house, a blade rack and a sister who said I would crawl home inside a year. Damn her, she was wrong, {to}.
Worst job ever? Six systems escorting a cargo of decorative pillows. Pillows! Not one pirate. I have never been so ashamed.
Always a warrior, {to}. Only the battlefield changed. Ships and blades before, the whole bloody galaxy now.
I thought only fools went exploring. Then I saw my first undiscovered star. Turns out I was the fool. A happy one.
Battles, bars and bad pay, {to}. Now it is stars, discoveries and bad coffee. Crap coffee, but an improvement.
